claims.statement: In Māori tradition, the Maero (or Mohoao) are an iwi-atua or supernatural people from New Zealand.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Māori, Maero (atau Mohoao) adalah iwi-atua atau kaum gaib dari New Zealand.
claims.quote: In Māori tradition, the Maero (or Mohoao) are an iwi-atua or supernatural people from New Zealand.

claims.statement: They are described as giants or wild men inhabiting mountains and forests in the South Island and Tararua Range.
claims.statement_id: Mereka digambarkan sebagai raksasa atau manusia liar hutan yang mendiami pegunungan dan hutan di South Island serta Tararua Range.
claims.quote: They are sometimes described as giants or wild men of the woods, and inhabit mountains and forest, particularly in the South Island and Tararua Range.

claims.statement: Maero are characterised as wild, malevolent and violent, carrying stone clubs as weapons.
claims.statement_id: Maero memiliki sifat liar, jahat, dan membawa gada batu sebagai senjata.
claims.quote: Maero are characterised as wild, malevolent and often violent, carrying stone clubs as weapons.

claims.statement: They are covered in dark body hair and have long bony fingers with sharp fingernails.
claims.statement_id: Tubuh mereka tertutup rambut hitam dan memiliki jari kurus panjang dengan kuku tajam.
claims.quote: They are covered in dark body hair and have long, bony fingers with sharp fingernails. They kill and eat humans and other animals.

claims.statement: The Maero harbor anger towards the Māori from Hawaiki for displacing them.
claims.statement_id: Maero menyimpan amarah terhadap suku Māori yang tiba dari Hawaiki karena telah menggusur mereka.
claims.quote: The Maero are said to harbour anger towards the Māori, who arrived from Hawaiki, and are thought to have displaced them and ruined the tapu (sacredness) of their homes, forcing them to dwell in inhospitable alpine regions.

claims.statement: Tukoio attacked a maero, cutting off its arms, legs and head.
claims.statement_id: Tukoio pernah menyerang seekor maero dan memotong lengan, kaki, serta kepalanya.
claims.quote: Tukoio, a mortal man, once found a maero, a mohoao (wild man), and attacked it, cutting off its arms, legs and head.

claims.statement: The head brought back was still alive and called for help.
claims.statement_id: Kepala maero yang dibawa ternyata masih hidup dan berseru meminta pertolongan.
claims.quote: He brought the head back, but it was still alive and called for help.

claims.statement: The maero put itself back together and returned to the forest.
claims.statement_id: Maero tersebut ternyata mampu menyatukan kembali tubuhnya dan kembali ke hutan.
claims.quote: Tukoio did not want to fight a whole clan of maero, so he dropped it and came back later with reinforcements, only to find the maero had put itself back together and returned to the forest.

claims.statement: Taylor records that the Maero, wild men of the woods, are said even yet to exist on mountains; a curl of smoke seen there is commonly attributed to the Maero, which he regards as evidence of their past rather than present existence.
claims.statement_id: Taylor mencatat bahwa Maero, manusia liar dari hutan, dikatakan masih ada di pegunungan; kepulan asap yang terlihat di sana lazim dianggap perbuatan Maero, tetapi ia memandangnya sebagai bukti keberadaan mereka di masa lalu, bukan masa kini.
claims.quote: as the Maero and Mohocto, or wild man of the woods ; they are said even yet to exist on the Tarama mountains ; if a cnrl of smoke should be seen upon them, it is commonly attributed to the Maero. This, however, is to be regarded as an evidence of their past, rather than present existence.

claims.statement: Tregear's dictionary defines maero (mythological) as an ogre or a wild man of the woods.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Tregear mendefinisikan maero (istilah mitologi) sebagai ogre atau manusia liar hutan.
claims.quote: MAERO (myth.), an ogre; a wild man of the woods.

claims.statement: Malingee is a nocturnal malignant Australian Aboriginal spirit.
claims.statement_id: Malingee adalah roh nokturnal jahat dalam mitologi Australian Aboriginal.
claims.quote: Malingee is a nocturnal malignant Australian Aboriginal spirit.

claims.statement: In Aboriginal mythology they avoid humans but when provoked slay mercilessly with a stone knife or axe.
claims.statement_id: Malingee menghindari manusia tetapi jika diganggu akan membunuh tanpa ampun dengan pisau batu atau kapak.
claims.quote: In Aboriginal mythology, they prefer to avoid humans, but when provoked, they will slay mercilessly with a stone knife or axe.

claims.statement: Malingees have stone knees that knock making a scraping sound, and eyes that smolder like coals.
claims.statement_id: Malingee memiliki lutut dari batu yang beradu menimbulkan bunyi derit dan mata membara bagai bara api.
claims.quote: Malingees have knees of stone that knock together, making a scraping sound, and have eyes that smolder like the coals of a cold fire.

claims.statement: These features made it possible for humans to detect and avoid nearby Malingees.
claims.statement_id: Ciri khas tersebut membantu manusia mengenali dan menghindari keberadaan Malingee.
claims.quote: These features were supposed to make it possible for humans to detect and avoid nearby Malingees.

claims.statement: The Manaia is a mythological creature in Māori culture, common in carving and jewellery.
claims.statement_id: Manaia adalah makhluk mitologi dalam budaya Māori dan motif umum dalam ukiran serta perhiasan.
claims.quote: The Manaia is a mythological creature in Māori culture, and is a common motif in Māori carving and jewellery.

claims.statement: The Manaia is usually depicted with bird head, fish tail, and human body.
claims.statement_id: Manaia biasanya digambarkan berkepala burung, berekor ikan, dan bertubuh manusia.
claims.quote: The Manaia is usually depicted as having the head of a bird and the tail of a fish and the body of a man, though it is sometimes depicted as a bird, a serpent, or a human figure in profile.

claims.statement: The Manaia is believed to be the messenger between mortals and spirits, and a guardian against evil.
claims.statement_id: Manaia dipercaya sebagai utusan antara dunia fana dan alam roh, serta simbol pelindung dari kejahatan.
claims.quote: The Manaia is traditionally believed to be the messenger between the earthly world of mortals and the domain of the spirits, and its symbol is used as a guardian against evil.

claims.statement: In this form it is represented in a figure-of-eight shape culminating in a bird-like beak.
claims.statement_id: Dalam wujud ini ia biasa digambarkan berbentuk angka delapan dengan paruh burung di bagian atasnya.
claims.quote: In this form, it is usually represented in a figure-of-eight shape, the upper half culminating in a bird-like beak.

claims.statement: Related Manaia-like symbols are found in other Polynesian cultures such as Hawaii.
claims.statement_id: Simbol serupa Manaia juga ditemukan dalam kebudayaan Polynesian lainnya seperti di Hawaii.
claims.quote: Related Manaia-like symbols are also found in other Polynesian cultures, such as in Hawaii and Easter Island.

claims.statement: Manaia designs are often depicted three-fingered representing birth, life, and death.
claims.statement_id: Desain Manaia sering berjarikan tiga yang melambangkan trinitas kelahiran, kehidupan, dan kematian.
claims.quote: Manaia designs vary subtly in form between iwi, though they are often depicted as three-fingered, with these digits representing the trinity of birth, life, and death.

claims.statement: Hamilton describes the Manaia as a lizard or snake form with several varieties, one of the most interesting being the snake form with the eagle's head.
claims.statement_id: Hamilton menyebut manaia sebagai bentuk kadal atau ular dengan beberapa varian; salah satu yang paling menarik ialah bentuk ular berkepala elang.
claims.quote: The Manaia, or lizard, or snake, is a remarkable deviation from the general law stated here. There are several varieties : probably the snake form with the eagle's head is one of the most interesting, carrying us back to some of the older mythologies.

claims.statement: On a board from a carved storehouse (pataka), conventional human figures alternate with bird-headed manaias.
claims.statement_id: Pada sebuah papan dari lumbung berukir (pataka), figur manusia yang konvensional berselang-seling dengan manaia berkepala burung.
claims.quote: A fine piece of old workmanship which formed part of a carved storehouse, or pataka. It represents the usual conventional figures of human beings, alternated with the bird-headed manaias.

claims.statement: Hamilton suggests that manaias may have been considered representations of lizards, and notes that in Samoa manaia is the name of a lizard.
claims.statement_id: Hamilton menduga manaia mungkin dianggap sebagai gambaran kadal, dan mencatat bahwa di Samoa manaia adalah nama seekor kadal.
claims.quote: Possibly these manaias may have been considered as representations of lizards. ... In Samoa, manaia is the name of a lizard.

claims.statement: Hamilton notes that a carving in bone or greenstone, probably representing the "seahorse" fish (Hippocampus; kiore moana in Māori), is called a manaia.
claims.statement_id: Hamilton mencatat bahwa ukiran dari tulang atau batu hijau yang kemungkinan menggambarkan ikan "kuda laut" (Hippocampus), kiore moana dalam bahasa Māori, disebut manaia.
claims.quote: Cook mentions seeing dried specimens of the fish known as the "seahorse" {Hippocampus), or the kiore moana of the Maori hanging at the ear. A carving, probably representing this fish, is sometimes seen in bone and in greenstone, and is called a manaia.

claims.statement: In Māori mythology, Matuku-tangotango is an ogre who kills Wahieroa son of Tāwhaki.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Māori, Matuku-tangotango adalah raksasa pembunuh Wahieroa putra Tāwhaki.
claims.quote: In Māori mythology, Matuku-tangotango (Matuku) is an ogre who kills Wahieroa the son of Tāwhaki.

claims.statement: In some versions, Matuku lives in a cave called Putawarenuku.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa versi, Matuku tinggal di dalam gua bernama Putawarenuku.
claims.quote: In some versions, Matuku lives in a cave called Putawarenuku.

claims.statement: Matuku's servant reveals that at the new moon his master can be killed at his washing pool.
claims.statement_id: Pelayan Matuku memberi tahu bahwa tuannya dapat dibunuh saat bulan baru di kolam tempat ia membasuh muka dan rambut.
claims.quote: He hears from Matuku's servant that at the new moon his master can be killed at the pool where he washes his face and hair.

claims.statement: When the new moon arrives, Rātā grabs the ogre by the hair at the pool and kills him.
claims.statement_id: Saat bulan baru tiba, Rātā menyergap sang raksasa ketika kepalanya di kolam dan membunuhnya.
claims.quote: When the new moon has come, Rātā waits until the ogre comes out of his cave and is leaning over with his head in the pool. He grabs him by the hair and kills him.

claims.statement: In Grey's collection, Wahieroa was slain treacherously by a chief named Matukutakotako; his son Rata was born some time before his death.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kumpulan Grey, Wahieroa dibunuh secara curang oleh seorang kepala suku bernama Matukutakotako; putranya Rata lahir beberapa waktu sebelum kematiannya.
claims.quote: Wahieroa was slain treacherously by a chief named Matukutakotako, but his son Rata was born some time before his death.

claims.statement: When asked where the man who killed his father was, the man left in charge of the place answered that he lives beneath the earth and, when the new moon appears, rises and comes forth upon the earth and devours men as his food.
claims.statement_id: Ditanya di mana pembunuh ayahnya, penjaga tempat itu menjawab bahwa orang itu tinggal di bawah tanah dan, saat bulan baru muncul, bangkit ke bumi serta melahap manusia sebagai makanannya.
claims.quote: Where is the man who killed my father ? ' The man who was left in charge of the place answered him : ' He lives beneath in the earth there, and I am left here by him, to call to him and warn him when the new moon appears ; at that season he rises and comes forth upon the earth, and devours men as his food.

claims.statement: Matukutakotako heard him, seized his two-handed wooden sword, rose up from the earth and went straight to his two fountains.
claims.statement_id: Matukutakotako mendengar seruan itu, mengambil pedang kayu bermata dua, bangkit dari dalam tanah, dan langsung menuju dua mata airnya.
claims.quote: And Matukutakotako heard him, and seizing his two-handed wooden sword, he rose up from the earth there, and went straight to his two fountains

claims.statement: As Matukutakotako raised his head from the water, Rata seized him by the hair with one hand and smote and slew him with the other, avenging the death of his father Wahieroa.
claims.statement_id: Saat Matukutakotako mengangkat kepalanya dari air, Rata menangkap rambutnya dengan satu tangan dan menebasnya dengan tangan yang lain hingga tewas, sehingga membalaskan kematian ayahnya Wahieroa.
claims.quote: as Matukutakotako raised his head from the water, Rata, with one hand seized him by the hair, while with the other he smote and slew him ; thus he avenged the death of his father Wahieroa.

claims.statement: Tregear's dictionary lists Matuku (mythological), also Matuku-tangotango or Matuku-takotako, as an ogre-chief and slayer of Wahieroa son of Tawhaki, who had an underground habitation, a cave called Putawarenuku.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Tregear mencatat Matuku (mitologi), juga Matuku-tangotango atau Matuku-takotako, sebagai kepala ogre pembunuh Wahieroa putra Tawhaki, yang berdiam di bawah tanah dalam gua bernama Putawarenuku.
claims.quote: MATUKU (myth.), or Matuku-tangotango, or Matuku-takotako, an ogre-chief, the slayer of Wahieroa the son of Tawhaki. Matuku had an underground habitation, a cave called Putawarenuku.

claims.statement: In Māori mythology, Māui is a culture hero, demigod, and trickster.
claims.statement_id: Māui adalah pahlawan budaya, manusia setengah dewa, dan trickster dalam mitologi Māori.
claims.quote: In Māori mythology, as in other Polynesian traditions, Māui is a culture hero, demigod and a trickster, famous for his exploits and cleverness.

claims.statement: He possessed superhuman strength and was capable of shapeshifting into birds and worms.
claims.statement_id: Ia memiliki kekuatan manusia super dan mampu mengubah wujud menjadi burung atau cacing.
claims.quote: He possessed superhuman strength, and was capable of shapeshifting into animals such as birds and worms.

claims.statement: Māui caught a giant fish using a jaw-bone hook which became the North Island of New Zealand.
claims.statement_id: Māui memancing ikan raksasa dengan kail tulang rahang neneknya yang menjadi Te Ika-a-Māui.
claims.quote: Māui is credited with catching a giant fish using a fishhook taken from his grandmother's jaw-bone; the giant fish would become the North Island of New Zealand, known as Te Ika-a-Māui.

claims.statement: In some traditions his canoe became the South Island, known as Te Waka a Māui.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa tradisi, perahunya menjadi South Island yang dikenal sebagai Te Waka a Māui.
claims.quote: In some traditions, his canoe (waka) became the South Island, known as Te Waka a Māui.

claims.statement: His last trick, which led to his death, involved the goddess Hine-nui-te-pō.
claims.statement_id: Tipuan terakhirnya yang berujung pada kematiannya melibatkan dewi Hine-nui-te-pō.
claims.quote: His last trick, which led to his death, involved the goddess Hine-nui-te-pō.

claims.statement: In Grey's collection, Māui proposes catching the sun in a noose to compel it to move more slowly so that mankind may have long days to labour in, then strikes it with his enchanted weapon with many blows.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kumpulan Grey, Māui mengajak saudara-saudaranya menjerat matahari agar bergerak lebih lambat sehingga manusia punya hari yang panjang untuk bekerja, lalu menyerangnya dengan senjata ajaibnya dan memukulnya berkali-kali.
claims.quote: Let us now catch the sun in a noose, so that we may compel him to move more slowly, in order that mankind may have long days to labour in to procure subsistence for themselves ... Then forth rushed that bold hero, Maui-tiki-tiki-o- Taranga, with his enchanted weapon. Alas ! the sun screams aloud ; he roars ; Maui strikes him fiercely with many blows

claims.statement: In Grey's collection, dry land hidden under the ocean was fished up by Māui with an enchanted fish-hook pointed with a bit of the jaw-bone of his ancestress.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kumpulan Grey, daratan yang tersembunyi di bawah laut dipancing naik oleh Māui dengan kail ajaib yang ujungnya dari sepotong tulang rahang leluhur perempuannya.
claims.quote: Thus was dry land fished up by Maui after it had been hidden under the ocean by Rangi and Ta- whiri-ma-tea. It was with an enchanted fish-hook that he drew it up, which was pointed with a bit of the jaw-bone of his ancestress Muri-ranga- whenua

claims.statement: The laughter of the little bird tiwakawaka woke the old woman, who opened her eyes, started up and killed Māui.
claims.statement_id: Tawa burung kecil tiwakawaka membangunkan perempuan tua itu, yang lalu membuka mata, bangkit, dan membunuh Māui.
claims.quote: at last, the little Tiwakawaka could no longer keep it in, and laughed out loud, with its merry cheerful note ; this woke the old woman up, she opened her eyes, started up, and killed Maui.

claims.statement: According to the traditions recorded by Grey, this was the cause of the introduction of death into the world; Hine-nui-te-po is the goddess of death, and had Māui passed safely through her, death itself would have been destroyed.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi yang dicatat Grey, peristiwa itu menjadi sebab masuknya kematian ke dunia; Hine-nui-te-po adalah dewi kematian, dan jika Māui melewatinya dengan selamat, kematian itu sendiri akan dihancurkan.
claims.quote: this was the cause of the introduction of death into the world (Hine-nui-te-po being the goddess of death : if Maui had passed safely through her, then no more human beings would have died, but death itself would have been destroyed)

claims.statement: Māui-tikitiki-a-Taranga is one of the names or epithets of Māui, meaning "Māui the top-knot of Taranga".
claims.statement_id: Māui-tikitiki-a-Taranga adalah salah satu nama atau julukan Māui, yang berarti "Māui jambul Taranga".
claims.quote: Māui-tikitiki-a-Taranga ("Māui the top-knot of Taranga")

claims.statement: A Nargun was a fierce half-human half-stone creature living in the Den of Nargun in Victoria, Australia.
claims.statement_id: Nargun adalah makhluk separuh manusia separuh batu yang tinggal di Den of Nargun di Victoria, Australia.
claims.quote: A Nargun, according to Gunai/Kurnai tribal legends, was a fierce half-human half-stone creature that lived in the Den of Nargun, a cave under a rock overhang behind a small waterfall located in the Mitchell River National Park, Victoria, Australia.

claims.statement: Aboriginal legend describes the Nargun as entirely made of stone except hands, arms and breast.
claims.statement_id: Legenda menggambarkan Nargun seluruhnya terbuat dari batu kecuali tangan, lengan, dan dadanya.
claims.quote: Aboriginal legend describes the Nargun as a beast entirely made of stone except for its hands, arms and breast.

claims.statement: The creature dragged unwary travellers into its den and weapons turned back on their owner.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini menyeret pengelana ke sarangnya dan senjata yang diarahkan padanya akan berbalik mengenai pemiliknya.
claims.quote: The fierce creature would drag unwary travellers into its den. Any weapon directed against it would be turned back on its owner.

claims.statement: Campfire stories told of Nargun abducting children who visited the rockpool.
claims.statement_id: Kisah api unggun menuturkan bagaimana Nargun menculik anak-anak yang mendatangi kolam batu.
claims.quote: Stories were told around aboriginal campfires about how the Nargun would abduct children who visited the rockpool.

claims.statement: Nargun could not be harmed with boomerangs or spears as they reflected back.
claims.statement_id: Nargun tidak dapat dilukai dengan bumerang atau tombak karena akan dipantulkan kembali.
claims.quote: It was said the Nargun could not be harmed with boomerangs or spears, as they would be reflected back to the thrower.

claims.statement: According to Gunaikurnai lore the Nargun is a large female creature who lives in a cave behind the waterfall.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi Gunaikurnai, Nargun adalah makhluk besar berjenis kelamin perempuan yang tinggal di sebuah gua di balik air terjun.
claims.quote: According to Gunaikurnai lore the Nargun is a large female creature who lives in a cave behind the waterfall.

claims.statement: The Den of Nargun on Woolshed Creek, a small tributary of the Mitchell River, is of great cultural significance and known as a women's place; it is a place of women's initiation and learning ceremonies, and traditionally Gunaikurnai men are not allowed to enter the area of the Den and the Woolshed Creek valley.
claims.statement_id: Den of Nargun di Woolshed Creek, anak sungai kecil Mitchell River, bermakna budaya besar dan dikenal sebagai tempat perempuan; di sana berlangsung inisiasi dan pembelajaran perempuan, dan secara tradisional lelaki Gunaikurnai tidak boleh memasuki kawasan itu dan lembah Woolshed Creek.
claims.quote: The Den of Nargun on Woolshed Creek, a small tributary of the Mitchell River, is of great cultural significance and is known as a women's place. ... It is a place of women's initiation and learning ceremonies, and traditionally Gunaikurnai men are not allowed to enter the area of the Den of Nargun and the Woolshed Creek valley.

claims.statement: Stories told around campfires said the Nargun would abduct children who wandered off on their own and could not be harmed with boomerangs or spears; the stories served to keep children close to the campsite and keep people away from the sacred cave.
claims.statement_id: Kisah di sekitar api unggun menceritakan Nargun menculik anak-anak yang berkeliaran sendirian dan tak dapat dilukai bumerang atau tombak; kisah itu berfungsi menjaga anak-anak tetap dekat perkemahan dan menjauhkan orang dari gua keramat.
claims.quote: Stories were told around campfires about how the Nargun would abduct children who wandered off on their own. The Nargun could not be harmed with boomerangs or spears. These stories served the dual purpose of keeping children close to the campsite and ensuring that people stayed away from the sacred cave.

claims.statement: Patupaiarehe are supernatural beings with fair skin and blonde or red hair, without tattoos.
claims.statement_id: Patupaiarehe adalah makhluk gaib berkulit pucat berambut pirang atau merah tanpa rajah tato.
claims.quote: Patupaiarehe are supernatural beings (he iwi atua) in Māori mythology that are described as pale to fair skinned with blonde hair or red hair, usually having the same stature as ordinary people, and never tattooed.

claims.statement: They are nocturnal or active on foggy days as direct sunlight can be fatal.
claims.statement_id: Mereka aktif di malam hari atau hari berkabut karena sinar matahari langsung dapat mematikan bagi mereka.
claims.quote: They can draw mist to themselves, but tend to be nocturnal or active on misty or foggy days as direct sunlight can be fatal to them.

claims.statement: They prefer raw food and have an aversion to steam and fire.
claims.statement_id: Mereka menyukai makanan mentah dan tidak menyukai uap serta api.
claims.quote: They prefer raw food and have an aversion to steam and fire.

claims.statement: Patupaiarehe live in deep forests and mountainous regions, hostile to human intruders.
claims.statement_id: Patupaiarehe hidup di hutan lebat dan wilayah pegunungan, serta dapat memusuhi manusia yang menyusup ke wilayah mereka.
claims.quote: Patupaiarehe can be hostile to humans, especially those who intrude on their lands. They are believed to live in deep forests and hilly or mountainous regions, in large guarded communities

claims.statement: The music of their kōauau and pūtōrino flutes reveals their presence on foggy days.
claims.statement_id: Musik seruling kōauau dan pūtōrino mereka kerap terdengar pada hari-hari berkabut.
claims.quote: The music of their kōauau and pūtōrino (bugle flutes), along with their singing of waiata occasionally reveals their presence on foggy days.

claims.statement: In a story recorded by Shortland, a Patupaiarehe or Fairy came to Ruarangi's house while he was away and carried his wife off to the hills.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat Shortland, seorang Patupaiarehe atau peri datang ke rumah Ruarangi saat ia pergi dan membawa istrinya ke perbukitan.
claims.quote: One day while Ruarangi was absent from his house a Patupaiarehe or Fairy came to it, and finding only the wife of Ruarangi within, carried her off to the hills.

claims.statement: In a story recorded by Shortland, a hill is said to have belonged to the Patupaiarehe or Fairies, who had a pa on the hill named Tuahu-o-te-atua.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah kisah yang dicatat Shortland, sebuah bukit disebut milik Patupaiarehe atau peri, yang memiliki sebuah pa di bukit itu bernama Tuahu-o-te-atua.
claims.quote: The hill belonged to the Patupaiarehe or Fairies. They had a Pa on the hill named Tuahu-o-te-atua.

claims.statement: In Grey's collection, Ngatoro-i-rangi visited the mountains and placed Patupaiarehe, or fairies, there.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kumpulan Grey, Ngatoro-i-rangi mengunjungi pegunungan dan menempatkan Patupaiarehe, atau peri, di sana.
claims.quote: Ngatoro-i-rangi went, how- ever, about the country, and where he found dry valleys ... he also visited the mountains, and placed Patupaiarehe, or fairies, there, and then returned to Maketu and dwelt there.

claims.statement: A chapter heading in Grey's collection states that the art of netting was learned by Kahukura from the fairies (patupaiarehe).
claims.statement_id: Judul sebuah bab dalam kumpulan Grey menyatakan bahwa seni menjala dipelajari Kahukura dari para peri (patupaiarehe).
claims.quote: THE ART OF NETTING LEARNED BY KAHUKURA FROM THE FAIRIES (ko te korero mo nga patupaiarehe)

claims.statement: Rogo-Tumu-Here was an octopus demon from Tuamotu mythology.
claims.statement_id: Rogo-Tumu-Here adalah iblis gurita dari mitologi Tuamotu.
claims.quote: Rogo-Tumu-Here was an octopus demon from Tuamotu mythology.

claims.statement: He swallowed Hina-Arau-Riki and was slain by Turi-A-Faumea and Tu-Nui-Ka-Rere.
claims.statement_id: Ia menelan Hina-Arau-Riki dan kemudian dibunuh oleh Turi-A-Faumea bersama Tu-Nui-Ka-Rere.
claims.quote: He attacked and swallowed Hina-Arau-Riki, the wife of Turi-A-Faumea, son of Tangaroa and Faumea, and was slain by the former males along with Tu-Nui-Ka-Rere.

claims.statement: In Beckwith's account, Turi makes Hina-a-rauriki his wife; as they go surfing, the demon octopus Rogo-tumu-here seizes Hina and carries her away to the bottom of the ocean.
claims.statement_id: Dalam catatan Beckwith, Turi menjadikan Hina-a-rauriki istrinya; saat mereka berselancar, gurita iblis Rogo-tumu-here menyambar Hina dan membawanya ke dasar samudra.
claims.quote: Turi makes Hina-a-rauriki his wife. They go surfing. The demon octopus Rogo-tumu-here seizes Hina and carries her away to the bottom of the ocean.

claims.statement: Tagaroa baits his hook with sacred red feathers and Rogo is drawn up into the canoe.
claims.statement_id: Tagaroa memasang kailnya dengan bulu merah sakral dan Rogo terangkat ke dalam perahu.
claims.quote: Tagaroa baits his hook with sacred red feathers and Rogo is drawn up into the canoe.

claims.statement: Tagaroa cuts off one tentacle after another until the head comes up; he cuts that off and Hina is drawn out from it covered with slime.
claims.statement_id: Tagaroa memotong tentakel satu demi satu hingga kepalanya muncul; ia memotong kepala itu dan Hina ditarik keluar darinya berlumur lendir.
claims.quote: One tentacle after another Tagaroa cuts off until the head comes up. Tagaroa cuts that off and Hina is drawn out from it covered with slime.

claims.statement: In Vahitahi of the Tuamotus, Faumea is an eel-woman; Tagaroa sleeps with her and she bears Tu-nui-ka-rere (or Ratu-nui) and Turi-a-faumea.
claims.statement_id: Di Vahitahi, Tuamotu, Faumea disebut perempuan-belut; Tagaroa tidur bersamanya dan ia melahirkan Tu-nui-ka-rere (atau Ratu-nui) dan Turi-a-faumea.
claims.quote: In Vahitahi of the Tuamotus, Faumea is an eel-woman ... Tagaroa sails to the land of Faumea. ... He sleeps with her and she bears Tu-nui-ka-rere (or Ratu-nui) and Turi-a-faumea.

claims.statement: In Māori mythology, Rongomai refers to several entities.

claims.quote: In Māori mythology, Rongomai refers to several entities:

claims.statement: Rongomai was the war god of tribes in the Lake Taupō region.
claims.statement_id: Rongomai adalah dewa perang suku-suku di kawasan Lake Taupō.
claims.quote: the war god of the tribes in the Lake Taupō region.

claims.statement: A being in whale form which attacked the war-party of Maru.
claims.statement_id: Entitas berwujud paus yang menyerang rombongan perang Maru.
claims.quote: a being in whale form which attacked and almost wiped out the war-party of Maru.

claims.statement: A celebrated demi-god ancestor who visited Miru in the underworld.
claims.statement_id: Leluhur setengah dewa yang mengunjungi Miru di dunia bawah untuk mempelajari mantra suci.
claims.quote: a celebrated demi-god ancestor of some iwi. He went with Ihinga and others of his friends to visit the dread Miru in her abode in the underworld.

claims.statement: A meteor or comet seen in broad daylight during the siege of Rangiuru at Ōtaki.
claims.statement_id: Meteor atau komet yang terlihat di siang hari saat pengepungan benteng Rangiuru di Ōtaki.
claims.quote: a meteor or comet, seen in the full light of day when in comparatively recent times, the Ngāti Hau tribe were besieging the fortress named Rangiuru at Ōtaki, occupied by the Ngāti Awa.

claims.statement: In Grey's collection, the women took by stealth the gods of the people, namely Maru, Te Iho-o-te-rangi, Rongomai, Itupawa and Haungaroa; having no canoe, they used these gods as a canoe to cross the sea.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kumpulan Grey, para perempuan mengambil secara diam-diam dewa-dewa kaum itu, yaitu Maru, Te Iho-o-te-rangi, Rongomai, Itupawa, dan Haungaroa; karena tanpa kano, dewa-dewa itu berfungsi sebagai kano untuk menyeberangi laut.
claims.quote: The women then took by stealth the gods of the people, that is to say, Maru, and Te Iho-o-te-rangi, and Rongomai, and Itupawa, and Haungaroa, and they had no canoe for their journey, but these gods served them as a canoe to cross the sea.

claims.statement: Te Wheke-a-Muturangi is a monstrous octopus destroyed in Tory Channel by Kupe.
claims.statement_id: Te Wheke-a-Muturangi adalah monster gurita yang dibunuh di Tory Channel oleh penjelajah Kupe.
claims.quote: In Māori mythology, Te Wheke-a-Muturangi is a monstrous octopus destroyed in Whekenui Bay, Tory Channel or at Pātea by Kupe the navigator.

claims.statement: The octopus was a pet or familiar of Muturangi, a powerful tohunga of Hawaiki.
claims.statement_id: Gurita tersebut adalah peliharaan Muturangi, seorang tohunga sakti dari Hawaiki.
claims.quote: The octopus was a pet or familiar of Muturangi, a powerful tohunga of Hawaiki. The wheke was nonetheless a wild creature and a guardian.

claims.statement: Kupe chased the giant octopus across Cook Strait to Tory Channel and cut off its arms with his adze.
claims.statement_id: Kupe mengejar gurita raksasa tersebut melintasi Cook Strait menuju Tory Channel dan memotong lengannya dengan beliung.
claims.quote: When Kupe reached New Zealand, he encountered the beast off Castlepoint. The giant octopus then fled across Cook Strait, and was chased by Kupe through Tory Channel. Here a great battle took place, and when the octopus appeared to be about to flee, Kupe cut off its arms with his adze, killing it

claims.statement: In Grey's collection, the great cuttle-fish or dragon that had fled from Castle Point was named by Kupe Te Wheke-a-Muturangi; it had fled to Tory Channel and was lying hid in this part of the current.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kumpulan Grey, cumi-cumi besar atau naga yang lari dari Castle Point dinamai Kupe Te Wheke-a-Muturangi; ia lari ke Tory Channel dan bersembunyi di bagian arus itu.
claims.quote: The great cuttle-fish or dragon, that had fled from Castle ... Point, which Kupe named Te Wheke-a-Muturangi ... had fled to Tory Channel, and was lying hid in this part of the current.

claims.statement: The monster heard the canoe of Kupe approaching and raised its arms above the waters to catch and devour the canoe, men and all.
claims.statement_id: Monster itu mendengar kano Kupe mendekat dan mengangkat lengannya dari air untuk menangkap dan melahap kano beserta seluruh awaknya.
claims.quote: The monster heard the canoe of Kupe approaching as they were pulling up the current, and raised its arms above the waters to catch and devour the canoe, men and all.

claims.statement: Kupe seized an immense hollow calabash and threw it overboard; hardly had it touched the water than the monster flew at it, thinking it was the canoe of Kupe.
claims.statement_id: Kupe mengambil sebuah labu besar berongga dan melemparkannya ke laut; begitu menyentuh air, monster itu menyerangnya karena mengira itu kano Kupe.
claims.quote: so Kupe seized an immense hollow calabash he had on board to carry his water in, and threw it overboard ; hardly had it touched the water ere the monster flew at it, thinking that it was the canoe of Kupe

claims.statement: Kupe, standing in his canoe in an excellent position to cut it with his axe, struck it a tremendous blow and severed it in two, killing it.
claims.statement_id: Kupe, yang berdiri di kanonya dalam posisi yang sangat baik untuk menebas, memukulnya dengan kapak dan membelahnya menjadi dua hingga mati.
claims.quote: Kupe, as he stood in his canoe, being in a most excellent position to cut it with his axe, seized the opportunity, and, striking; it a tremendous blow, he severed it in two, and killed it

claims.statement: In the mythology of the Adnyamathanha people from the Flinders Ranges, Akurra is a great snake deity.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi penduduk pribumi South Australia suku Adnyamathanha di Flinders Ranges, Akurra adalah dewa ular agung.
claims.quote: In the mythology of the Aboriginal people of South Australia (specifically, the Adnyamathanha people from the Flinders Ranges), Akurra is a great snake deity, sometimes associated with the Rainbow Serpent.

claims.statement: Adnyamathanha elders describe it as a giant water snake with a beard mane, scales and sharp fangs shaping the land.
claims.statement_id: Tetua Adnyamathanha menggambarkan Akurra sebagai ular air raksasa bersurai janggut, bersisik, bertaring tajam, yang gerakannya membentuk tanah.
claims.quote: Adnyamathanha elders describe it as a giant water snake with a beard mane, scales and sharp fangs, whose movements shaped the land.

claims.statement: Akurra is associated with the power of the shaman, and nobody else may go near him with impunity.
claims.statement_id: Akurra berhubungan dengan kekuatan dukun (shaman) dan tidak ada orang lain yang boleh mendekatinya tanpa bahaya.
claims.quote: Akurra is associated with the power of the shaman, and nobody else may go near him with impunity.

claims.statement: Akurra is also connected with water and rain.
claims.statement_id: Akurra juga terhubung dengan air dan hujan.
claims.quote: Akurra is also connected with water and rain.

claims.statement: During severe drought shamans visited Akurra's cave and heated his kidney fat over coals to bring rain.
claims.statement_id: Saat kemarau parah para dukun mendatangi gua Akurra dan memanaskan lemak ginjalnya di atas bara api untuk mendatangkan hujan.
claims.quote: According to one Adnyamathanha story, at times of severe drought the shamans would travel to the cave in which Akurra lived, draw the entire snake out and take his kidney fat, which they heated over a fire, allowing the melted fat to fall over the heated coals.

claims.statement: According to the Yura Muda, powerful Creation serpents known as Akurra created many features of the Flinders Ranges landscape.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Yura Muda, ular pencipta yang perkasa bernama Akurra menciptakan banyak ciri lanskap Flinders Ranges.
claims.quote: According to the Yura Muda, powerful Creation serpents known as Akurra created many features of the Flinders Ranges landscape.

claims.statement: The bodies of two Akurra form the walls of Ikara-Wilpena Pound.
claims.statement_id: Tubuh dua Akurra membentuk dinding Ikara-Wilpena Pound.
claims.quote: The bodies of two Akurra form the walls of Ikara-Wilpena Pound.

claims.statement: Akurra Adnya (Arkaroo Rock) is a significant Adnyamathanha painting site that depicts aspects of the Yura Muda (stories).
claims.statement_id: Akurra Adnya (Arkaroo Rock) adalah situs lukisan Adnyamathanha yang penting dan menggambarkan aspek-aspek Yura Muda (kisah).
claims.quote: Akurra Adnya (Arkaroo Rock) is a significant Adnyamathanha painting site that depicts aspects of the Yura Muda (stories)

claims.statement: The Canterbury Panther or Canterbury Cat is a New Zealand urban legend about a black panther in the Canterbury Region.
claims.statement_id: Canterbury Panther atau Canterbury Cat adalah legenda urban New Zealand tentang kumbang hitam di Canterbury Region.
claims.quote: The Canterbury Panther or Canterbury Cat is a New Zealand urban legend about a black panther which is said to live in the Canterbury Region.

claims.statement: Sightings of the animal go back to before the 1970s.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan hewan tersebut telah ada sejak sebelum era 1970-an.
claims.quote: Sightings of the animal go back to before the 1970s.

claims.statement: The Canterbury Panther made headlines in July 1977 when Frances Clark alleged seeing a tiger outside her home.
claims.statement_id: Canterbury Panther menjadi berita utama pada Juli 1977 ketika Frances Clark mengaku melihat harimau di luar rumahnya.
claims.quote: The Canterbury Panther first made headlines in July 1977, when Kaiapoi resident Frances Clark alleged that she had seen a tiger outside her home.

claims.statement: The most common explanation attributes sightings to mistaken identity of large feral black cats.
claims.statement_id: Penjelasan paling umum mengaitkannya dengan salah identifikasi kucing liar berukuran besar berbulu hitam.
claims.quote: The most common explanation for sightings of the Canterbury Panther are attributed to the mistaken identity of unusually large, feral cats with black fur.

claims.statement: Clark was initially discredited until sizeable paw prints and large droppings were found on a nearby beach in the following days; a military grade search was launched across land and sky, but no giant cat was found.
claims.statement_id: Clark mula-mula tidak dipercaya, sampai jejak kaki besar dan kotoran besar ditemukan di pantai terdekat beberapa hari kemudian; pencarian berkelas militer dilancarkan lewat darat dan udara, tetapi tidak ada kucing raksasa yang ditemukan.
claims.quote: Clark was initially discredited, until sizeable paw prints and large droppings were found on a nearby beach in the days following. A military grade search was launched across land and sky, but no giant cat was found.

claims.statement: Things remained relatively quiet until the late 90s, when a woman spotted a black cat "the size of a Labrador" in 1996 and a sighting of a black panther was reported in Mackenzie Country in 1999.
claims.statement_id: Keadaan relatif tenang sampai akhir 1990-an, ketika seorang perempuan melihat kucing hitam "sebesar Labrador" pada 1996 dan penampakan panther hitam dilaporkan di Mackenzie Country pada 1999.
claims.quote: Things remained relatively quiet until the late 90s, when a woman spotted a black cat "the size of a Labrador" in 1996, and another sighting of a black panther was reported in Mackenzie Country in 1999.

claims.statement: The panther became the perfect addition to Timpson's family adventure film Bookworm.
claims.statement_id: Sang panther menjadi tambahan yang sempurna bagi film petualangan keluarga Timpson, Bookworm.
claims.quote: That sense of wonder is why the panther became the perfect addition to Timpson's family adventure film Bookworm

claims.statement: According to the NZ Skeptics author, despite decades of sightings no one has provided verifiable proof: no carcasses, no clear photographs or videos, and very little physical trace evidence, like paw prints, that could be definitively linked to a panther.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis NZ Skeptics, meski bertahun-tahun ada penampakan, belum ada yang memberikan bukti yang dapat diverifikasi: tanpa bangkai, foto atau video yang jelas, dan hampir tanpa jejak fisik yang dapat dikaitkan dengan seekor panther.
claims.quote: Despite decades of sightings, no one has ever provided verifiable proof-no carcasses, no clear photographs or videos, and very little in the way of physical trace evidence, like paw prints that could be definitively linked to a panther.

claims.statement: Skeptical analysis of the sightings suggests that the mysterious panther may be nothing more than a combination of mis-identifications, myth-making and the power of suggestion.
claims.statement_id: Analisis skeptis atas penampakan itu menyimpulkan bahwa panther misterius mungkin hanya gabungan salah identifikasi, pembuatan mitos, dan kekuatan sugesti.
claims.quote: Skeptical analysis of these sightings suggests that the mysterious panther may be nothing more than a combination of mis-identifications, myth-making, and the power of suggestion.

claims.statement: Faumea is a figure in Polynesian mythology in the Tuamotus archipelago regarded as an eel-woman.
claims.statement_id: Faumea adalah tokoh mitologi Polinesia di kepulauan Tuamotu yang dipandang sebagai wanita-belut.
claims.quote: Faumea is a figure in Polynesian mythology, specifically that of the Tuamotus archipelago of French Polynesia, where she is regarded as an "eel-woman".

claims.statement: The sea god Tangaroa encounters her when he sails to her island.
claims.statement_id: Dewa laut Tangaroa menemuinya ketika berlayar ke pulaunya.
claims.quote: The sea god Tangaroa encounters her when he sails to her island.

claims.statement: Faumea bears Tangaroa two sons: Tu-Nui-Ka-Rere and Turi-A-Faumea.
claims.statement_id: Faumea melahirkan dua putra bagi Tangaroa yaitu Tu-Nui-Ka-Rere dan Turi-A-Faumea.
claims.quote: Faumea bears Tangaroa two sons: Tu-Nui-Ka-Rere (also called Rata-Nui) and Turi-A-Faumea.

claims.statement: Turi-A-Faumea's wife Hina-Arau-Riki is kidnapped by the octopus-demon Rogo-Tumu-Here.
claims.statement_id: Istri Turi-A-Faumea yang bernama Hina-Arau-Riki diculik oleh iblis gurita Rogo-Tumu-Here.
claims.quote: Later, Turi-A-Faumea's wife Hina-Arau-Riki is kidnapped by the octopus-demon Rogo-Tumu-Here.

claims.statement: In Beckwith's account, Tagaroa sails to the land of Faumea; Faumea is a woman who has eels in her body which kill men, but she teaches Tagaroa how to entice them outside.
claims.statement_id: Dalam catatan Beckwith, Tagaroa berlayar ke negeri Faumea; Faumea adalah perempuan yang memiliki belut di dalam tubuhnya yang membunuh laki-laki, tetapi ia mengajari Tagaroa cara memancing belut itu keluar.
claims.quote: Tagaroa sails to the land of Faumea. Faumea is a woman who has eels in her vagina which kill men, but she teaches Tagaroa how to entice them outside.

claims.statement: Faumea withdraws the wind into the sweat of her armpit and Tagaroa utters a chant for its release; Tagaroa bids Faumea catch the girdle of Tu-nui-ka-rere, who slips away into the sky and is lost to her.
claims.statement_id: Faumea menarik angin ke dalam keringat ketiaknya dan Tagaroa melantunkan mantra untuk melepaskannya; Tagaroa meminta Faumea menangkap ikat pinggang Tu-nui-ka-rere, yang menyelinap ke langit dan hilang darinya.
claims.quote: Faumea withdraws the wind into the sweat of her armpit and Tagaroa utters a chant for its release. He bids Faumea catch the girdle of Tu-nui-ka-rere, who slips away into the sky and is lost to her.

claims.statement: In Beckwith's discussion of Haumea, Haumea in Tahiti is the ogress Nona, ancestress of the Tafa'i group, and Faumea in Vahitahi of the Tuamotus is an eel-woman.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pembahasan Beckwith tentang Haumea, Haumea di Tahiti adalah raksasa perempuan Nona, leluhur kelompok Tafa'i, dan Faumea di Vahitahi, Tuamotu, adalah perempuan-belut.
claims.quote: In Tahiti, Haumea is the ogress Nona, ancestress of the Tafa'i group. ... In Vahitahi of the Tuamotus, Faumea is an eel-woman

claims.statement: According to Beckwith, Stimson tells the story from Anaa in the Tuamotus of Gana, Huri-te-papa and the princess Faumea, in which Gana is the suitor of Faumea in Tahiti-nui but Huri-te-papa wins her by his dancing.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Beckwith, Stimson menuturkan kisah dari Anaa di Tuamotu tentang Gana, Huri-te-papa, dan putri Faumea: Gana melamar Faumea di Tahiti-nui, tetapi Huri-te-papa memenangkannya lewat tariannya.
claims.quote: Stimson tells the story from Anaa in the Tuamotus of Gana, Huri-te-papa, and the princess Faumea, where Gana is the suitor of Faumea in Tahiti-nui, but Huri-te-papa wins her by his dancing.

claims.statement: Hakawai, also Hōkioi in the North Island, was a mythological bird sometimes heard but not usually seen.
claims.statement_id: Hakawai atau Hōkioi adalah burung mitologis bangsa Māori yang kerap terdengar namun jarang terlihat.
claims.quote: Hakawai, also Hōkioi  in the North Island, was to the New Zealand Māori people, a mythological bird that was sometimes heard but not usually seen.

claims.statement: Hakawai was one of eleven tapu birds of wind god Raka-maomao living in the heavens and descending at night.
claims.statement_id: Hakawai adalah salah satu dari sebelas burung tapu dewa angin Raka-maomao yang tinggal di langit dan turun ke bumi saat malam.
claims.quote: In Māori mythology the Hakawai was one of eleven tapu (sacred) birds of Raka-maomao, a god of wind.  The Hakawai lived in the heavens and only descended to the earth at night.

claims.statement: Hearing the Hakawai was considered a bad omen traditionally presaging war.
claims.statement_id: Mendengar suara Hakawai dianggap sebagai pertanda buruk yang menandakan datangnya perang.
claims.quote: Hearing the Hakawai was considered to be a bad omen, traditionally presaging war.

claims.statement: It was considered a gigantic bird of prey described by a Ngāti Apa chief.
claims.statement_id: Burung ini dipandang sebagai pemangsa raksasa yang digambarkan oleh kepala suku Ngāti Apa.
claims.quote: It was considered to be a gigantic bird of prey and was described (as the Hōkioi) by a Ngāti Apa chief, to the Governor of New Zealand Sir George Grey

claims.statement: The sound of Hakawai had two components: a vocal call hakwai followed by a high-speed non-vocal roar.
claims.statement_id: Suara Hakawai digambarkan memiliki dua unsur yaitu panggilan vokal hakwai diikuti deru gemuruh cepat.
claims.quote: There the sound ascribed to the Hakawai was described as having two main components, the first part being vocal, a call rendered as hakwai, hakwai, hakwai, followed by a non-vocal roar as of an object travelling through the air at high speed.

claims.statement: The hakawai was one of the 11 tapu (sacred) birds of Rakamaomao (the wind) and was said to have been a descendant of Tangaroa (god of the ocean) and Rehua (the star Antares, guardian of the uppermost heaven).
claims.statement_id: Hakawai adalah salah satu dari 11 burung tapu (sakral) Rakamaomao (angin) dan dikatakan keturunan Tangaroa (dewa laut) dan Rehua (bintang Antares, penjaga langit tertinggi).
claims.quote: The hakawai was one of the 11 tapu (sacred) birds of Rakamaomao (the wind) and was said to have been a descendant of Tangaroa (god of the ocean) and Rehua (the star Antares, guardian of the uppermost heaven)

claims.statement: In Maori legends and proverbs, the hakawai was a mythical bird dwelling afar in celestial space and only descending to earth at night.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda dan peribahasa Māori, hakawai adalah burung mitos yang berdiam jauh di angkasa dan hanya turun ke bumi pada malam hari.
claims.quote: In Maori legends and proverbs, the hakawai was a mythical bird dwelling afar in celestial space and only descending to earth at night.

claims.statement: A proverb quoted in the source likens a bird to the Hakawai, which makes itself invisible.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah peribahasa yang dikutip menyamakan sebuah burung dengan Hakawai, yang membuat dirinya tak terlihat.
claims.quote: (that bird is like the Hakawai, it makes itself invisible)

claims.statement: The most widely quoted legend about hokioi refers to a competition between hokioi and kahu (the hawk) to see who could fly the highest; the story explains why hokioi descends only at night and why he calls out his name.
claims.statement_id: Legenda hokioi yang paling banyak dikutip berkisah tentang perlombaan antara hokioi dan kahu (elang) untuk melihat siapa yang dapat terbang paling tinggi; kisah ini menjelaskan mengapa hokioi hanya turun pada malam hari dan mengucapkan namanya.
claims.quote: The most widely quoted legend about hokioi refers to a competition between hokioi and kahu (the hawk) to see who could fly the highest. This story explains why hokioi descends only at night and why he calls out his name.

claims.statement: The call of the hakawai was heard on calm moonlit nights and came from a great height.
claims.statement_id: Panggilan hakawai terdengar pada malam berbulan yang tenang dan datang dari ketinggian.
claims.quote: The call was heard on calm moonlit nights and came from a great height.

claims.statement: Miskelly's data support the hypothesis that the hakawai was a snipe.
claims.statement_id: Data penelitian Miskelly mendukung hipotesis bahwa hakawai adalah burung snipe.
claims.quote: These data support the hakawai = snipe hypothesis.

claims.statement: Tregear's dictionary lists hokioi as the name of an extinct or mythical bird; the Natives say it was a huge bird of prey, large as the moa, with many-coloured feathers and a bunch of red feathers on its head.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Tregear mencatat hokioi sebagai nama burung punah atau mitos; menurut penutur Māori ia burung pemangsa raksasa sebesar moa, berbulu warna-warni dengan seikat bulu merah di kepalanya.
claims.quote: HOKIOI {hokioi), the name of an extinct or mythical bird ... The Natives say that it was (like the Arabian Roc) a huge bird of prey, large as the moa (Dinornis) ; also that it had many-coloured feathers, and a bunch of red feathers on its head.

claims.statement: According to Tregear, Sir W. Buller considers the Hokioi to be identical with the Great Frigate Bird (Fregata aquila).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Tregear, Sir W. Buller menganggap Hokioi identik dengan Great Frigate Bird (Fregata aquila).
claims.quote: Sir W. Buller considers the Hokioi to be iden- tical with the Great Frigate Bird (Fregata aquila).

claims.quote: The hoop snake is a legendary creature of the United States, Canada, and Australia.

claims.statement: A hoop snake grasps its tail in its jaws and rolls after prey like a wheel.
claims.statement_id: Ciri khas hoop snake adalah menggigit ekornya sendiri dan menggelinding mengejar mangsa seperti roda.
claims.quote: According to folklore, the distinguishing feature of a hoop snake is that it can grasp its tail in its jaws, like the ouroboros of Greek mythology, and roll after its prey like a wheel.

claims.statement: The snake straightens out at the last second, skewering its victim with a venomous tail.
claims.statement_id: Ular ini meluruskan diri di detik terakhir untuk menusuk korbannya dengan ekor berbisa.
claims.quote: In one version of the myth, the snake straightens out at the last second, skewering its victim with its venomous tail.

claims.statement: An Australian rendition describes a circular snake with elongated spines along the inner lining.
claims.statement_id: Versi Australia menggambarkan ular bundar dengan duri memanjang di bagian dalam lingkar tubuhnya.
claims.quote: An Australian rendition of the myth describes a circular-shaped snake roughly the size of a steering wheel with a set of elongated spines evenly spaced along the inner lining of its circular-shaped body.

claims.statement: The "hoop snake" tale, as quoted from a herpetology book, is usually applied to the mud snake (Farancia abacura) and the rainbow snake (Farancia erytrogramma); supposedly the snake takes its tail into its mouth, forms a hoop and rolls after the nearest human, then tries to "sting" with its tail; if it jabs a tree instead, the plant immediately wilts and dies.
claims.statement_id: Dikutip dari buku herpetologi, kisah "hoop snake" biasanya dikenakan pada mud snake (Farancia abacura) dan rainbow snake (Farancia erytrogramma); konon ular itu memasukkan ekornya ke mulut, membentuk lingkaran, dan berguling mengejar manusia terdekat, lalu mencoba "menyengat" dengan ekornya; jika menusuk pohon, tanaman itu langsung layu dan mati.
claims.quote: The 'hoop snake' tale is usually applied to the mud snake [Farancia abacura] and to the rainbow snake [Farancia erytrogramma]. Supposedly, the snake takes its tail into its mouth, forms a hoop, and rolls after the nearest human. It then tries to 'sting' the person with its tail. Should the snake jab a tree instead, the poor plant immediately wilts and dies.

claims.statement: According to the column, a hoop/mud snake cannot sting with its tail, but it has a hard spine there that can draw blood when thrashed vigorously.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kolom itu, hoop snake atau mud snake tidak dapat menyengat dengan ekornya, tetapi memiliki duri keras di sana yang dapat melukai hingga berdarah bila dikibaskan dengan kuat.
claims.quote: While a hoop/mud snake cannot sting with its tail, it does have a hard spine back there that can draw blood when thrashed vigorously.

claims.statement: A historical marker inscription states that for generations local legend tells of an enormous snake that grasped its tail in its mouth and rolled down this hill toward its victims.
claims.statement_id: Prasasti penanda sejarah menyatakan bahwa selama beberapa generasi legenda setempat bercerita tentang ular raksasa yang menggigit ekornya dan berguling menuruni bukit ini ke arah korbannya.
claims.quote: FOR GENERATIONS, LOCAL LEGEND TELLS OF AN ENORMOUS SNAKE THAT GRASPED ITS TAIL IN ITS MOUTH AND ROLLED DOWN THIS HILL TOWARD ITS VICTIMS.

claims.statement: According to the marker description, the hoop snake rolls toward its victims and at the final moment straightens out its body and lashes out with its spiked tail.
claims.statement_id: Menurut uraian penanda itu, hoop snake berguling ke arah korbannya dan pada saat terakhir meluruskan tubuhnya lalu menyerang dengan ekornya yang berduri.
claims.quote: The hoop snake rolls toward its victims, and at the final moment straightens out its body and lashes out with its spiked tail.

claims.statement: The ipilja-ipilja is a giant gecko in Anindilyakwa mythology and creator of rain and thunder.
claims.statement_id: Ipilja-ipilja adalah tokek raksasa dalam mitologi suku Anindilyakwa di Australia dan pencipta hujan serta petir.
claims.quote: The ipilja-ipilja, or ipilya, is a giant gecko in the mythology of the Anindilyakwa people  of Australia. He is considered to be the creator of rain and thunder.

claims.statement: Ipilja-ipilja lives with his family in the Numarika swamp on Groote Eylandt.
claims.statement_id: Ipilja-ipilja hidup bersama keluarganya di rawa Numarika di muara Angoroko River di Groote Eylandt.
claims.quote: The ipilja-ipilja lives with his family, all giant geckos, in the Numarika swamp at the mouth of the Angoroko River of Groote Eylandt.

claims.statement: The gecko is about a hundred feet long, highly colored, with long hair and whiskers.
claims.statement_id: Tokek ini memiliki panjang sekitar seratus kaki dengan warna mencolok serta rambut dan kumis panjang.
claims.quote: The geckos are all "highly colored," with the ipilja-ipilja being about a hundred feet long and adorned with long hair and whiskers.

claims.statement: At the start of the monsoon season, he eats grass, drinks swamp water, and spews it into the sky.
claims.statement_id: Pada awal musim monsun, ia memakan rumput dan meminum air rawa lalu menyemburkannya ke langit.
claims.quote: At the beginning of the monsoon season, the ipilja-ipilja eats the grasses on the edge of the swamp and drinks a large quantity of the swamp water. He then spews the mixture into the sky.

claims.statement: The water becomes clouds bound by grass, and his roar becomes thunder.
claims.statement_id: Air berubah menjadi awan dan rumput mengikatnya, lalu auman Ipilja-ipilja menjadi petir.
claims.quote: The water turns into clouds, and the grass binds the clouds together. The ipilja-ipilja, pleased with his efforts, lets out a roar that becomes thunder.

claims.statement: On Groote Eylandt, northeastern Australia, the ipilja-ipilja is the colorful gecko who replaces the Rainbow Serpent.
claims.statement_id: Di Groote Eylandt, Australia timur laut, ipilja-ipilja adalah tokek berwarna-warni yang menggantikan Rainbow Serpent.
claims.quote: On Groote Eylandt, northeastern Australia, the colorful gecko who replaces the Rainbow Serpent.

claims.statement: Ipilja-ipilja creates storms, thunder and the monsoon rains.
claims.statement_id: Ipilja-ipilja menciptakan badai, guntur, dan hujan monsun.
claims.quote: Ipilja-ipilja creates storms, thunder, and the monsoon rains.

claims.statement: In Hawaiian mythology, Kaupe is a malevolent spirit calling out to lure victims to death, formerly ruling Nu'uanu Valley.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Hawaii, Kaupe adalah roh jahat yang memanggil orang di malam hari menuju kematian dan pernah menguasai Nu'uanu Valley.
claims.quote: In Hawaiian mythology, Kaupe is a malevolent spirit that calls out to people at night to lure them to their deaths. According to legend, he used to rule Nu'uanu Valley.

claims.statement: During his reign, Kaupe ate people on Oahu and Maui.
claims.statement_id: Selama masa kekuasaannya, Kaupe memakan manusia di Oahu lalu di Maui.
claims.quote: During his reign, Kaupe ate people on Oahu, then Maui.

claims.statement: Kaupe appears as an enormous man with a canine head and sharp claws.
claims.statement_id: Kaupe berwujud pria raksasa dengan kepala anjing dan cakar-cakar tajam.
claims.quote: According to mythology, Kaupe appears as an enormous man with a canine head and sharp claws.

claims.statement: Though from Nuuanu Valley, he is often encountered under Kipapa Bridge.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun berasal dari Lembah Nuuanu, ia kerap ditemui di bawah Jembatan Kipapa.
claims.quote: Though he is said to originally be from Nuuanu Valley, he is more often encountered under Kipapa Bridge.

claims.statement: Kaupe is considered a calling ghost because he mimics the sound of wounded or dying people to lure victims.
claims.statement_id: Kaupe disebut hantu pemanggil karena menirukan suara rintihan orang terluka atau sekarat untuk memikat mangsanya.
claims.quote: Kaupe is often considered a "calling ghost" because he calls to his victims rather than searching them out or coming across them by coincidence. His technique is to mimic the sound of numerous wounded or dying people.

claims.statement: Among dog-men represented as overthrowing the chief of a district and terrorizing the country, the most famous is the cannibal dog-man Kaupe, who overthrew the government of Ka-hanai-a-ke-akua and ruled the land from Nu'uanu to the sea.
claims.statement_id: Di antara manusia-anjing yang digambarkan menggulingkan kepala suatu distrik dan meneror negeri, yang paling terkenal ialah manusia-anjing kanibal Kaupe, yang menggulingkan pemerintahan Ka-hanai-a-ke-akua dan memerintah negeri dari Nu'uanu sampai ke laut.
claims.quote: Among dog-men represented as overthrowing the chief of a district and terrorizing the country, the most famous is the cannibal dog-man Kaupe who overthrew the government of Ka-hanai-a-ke-akua (Reared by the gods) and ruled the land from Nu'uanu to the sea.

claims.statement: Kaupe lives at Lihue on Oahu; he never attacks a high chief but eats some of the people both of Oahu and Maui, then crosses over to Hawaii and brings back a chief's son to sacrifice in the heiau at Lihue.
claims.statement_id: Kaupe tinggal di Lihue di Oahu; ia tidak pernah menyerang kepala suku tinggi tetapi memakan sebagian penduduk Oahu dan Maui, lalu menyeberang ke Hawaii dan membawa pulang putra seorang kepala suku untuk dikorbankan di heiau di Lihue.
claims.quote: Kaupe lives at Lihue on Oahu. He never attacks a high chief but eats some of the people both of Oahu and Maui. At last he crosses over to Hawaii and brings back a chief's son to sacrifice in the heiau at Lihue.

claims.statement: The prayer unfastens the boy's fetters, and father and son flee and hide under a rock at Moanalua while Kaupe goes on to look for them on Hawaii; the father learns the prayer for killing an enemy and overcomes Kaupe on Hawaii.
claims.statement_id: Doa itu membuka belenggu sang anak, ayah dan anak melarikan diri dan bersembunyi di bawah batu di Moanalua sementara Kaupe mencari mereka di Hawaii; sang ayah mempelajari doa untuk membunuh musuh dan mengalahkan Kaupe di Hawaii.
claims.quote: The prayer unfastens the boy's fetters and father and son flee and hide under a rock at Moanalua while Kaupe goes on to look for them on Hawaii. The father learns the prayer for killing an enemy, and overcomes Kaupe on Hawaii.

claims.statement: As a ghost god resting in the clouds stretched over the mountaintops of the Koolau range on Oahu, Kaupe's spirit body is today confused with legends of a dog-like creature called Poki, spotted or brindled in color and very long in body, who guards a certain section outside Honolulu.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai dewa hantu yang beristirahat di awan di atas puncak-puncak pegunungan Koolau di Oahu, tubuh roh Kaupe kini dikacaukan dengan legenda makhluk mirip anjing bernama Poki, berbintik atau belang dan sangat panjang tubuhnya, yang menjaga suatu bagian di luar Honolulu.
claims.quote: As a ghost god resting in the clouds stretched over the mountaintops of the Koolau range on Oahu, Kaupe's spirit body is today confused with legends of a dog-like creature called Poki, spotted or brindled in color and very long in body, who guards a certain section outside Honolulu

claims.statement: Kurangaituku is a part-woman part-bird supernatural being in Māori mythology told by Te Arawa and Raukawa iwi.
claims.statement_id: Kurangaituku adalah makhluk gaib separuh wanita dan separuh burung dalam mitologi Māori yang diceritakan oleh suku Te Arawa dan Raukawa.
claims.quote: Kurangaituku is a part-woman part-bird supernatural being in Māori mythology as told by the iwi (tribes) of Te Arawa and Raukawa.

claims.statement: Hatupatu was caught and taken to her cave, imprisoned with pet birds and lizards.
claims.statement_id: Hatupatu ditangkap dan dibawa ke gua Kurangaituku tempat ia dikurung bersama burung dan kadal peliharaan.
claims.quote: He runs away from her but is caught and taken to her cave, where he is imprisoned along with other pet birds and lizards.

claims.statement: Hatupatu destroyed her pet lizards and birds and stole her treasured korowai feather cloaks.
claims.statement_id: Hatupatu memusnahkan kadal dan burung peliharaan serta mencuri jubah bulu korowai milik Kurangaituku.
claims.quote: One day while Kurangaituku is out hunting, Hatupatu uses her taiaha (traditional weapon) to destroy her pet lizards and birds and steals her treasured korowai (feather cloaks).

claims.statement: At Whakarewarewa, Kurangaituku went through boiling mud pools and was burned to death.
claims.statement_id: Di Whakarewarewa, Kurangaituku masuk ke dalam kolam lumpur mendidih dan tewas terbakar.
claims.quote: When Hatupatu reaches Whakarewarewa, he is able to dodge around the boiling mud pools; Kurangaituku goes through them and is burned to death.

claims.statement: Kurangaituku is also sometimes known as Hine-ingoingo.
claims.statement_id: Kurangaituku terkadang juga dikenal dengan nama Hine-ingoingo.
claims.quote: Kurangaituku is also sometimes known as Hine-ingoingo.

claims.statement: Tregear's dictionary lists Kurangaituku as an Ogress who had wings on her arms, could spear birds with her lips and lived on raw food.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Tregear mencatat Kurangaituku sebagai ogress yang bersayap pada lengannya, dapat menombak burung dengan bibirnya, dan hidup dari makanan mentah.
claims.quote: KURANGAITUKU (myth.), an Ogress who had wings on her arms, could spear birds with her lips, and lived on raw food.

claims.statement: She found the youth Hatupatu and took him to her home; he disliked the uncooked food and induced the fairy to go farther and farther away each day hunting while he stayed at home cooking for himself.
claims.statement_id: Ia menemukan pemuda Hatupatu dan membawanya ke rumahnya; Hatupatu tidak suka makanan mentah dan membujuk sang peri pergi makin jauh setiap hari untuk berburu sementara ia tinggal di rumah memasak untuk dirinya sendiri.
claims.quote: She found the youth, Hatupatu, and took him to her home. He disliked the uncooked food, and induced the fairy to go farther and farther away each day hunting, while he stayed at home, cooking for himself

claims.statement: A bird went and told Kurangaituku, who flew after her truant.
claims.statement_id: Seekor burung pergi memberi tahu Kurangaituku, yang lalu terbang mengejar si pelarian.
claims.quote: A bird went and told Kurangaituku, who flew after her truant

claims.statement: In Grey's collection, she made only three strides before she reached her cave, and when she looked about she could see nothing in it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kumpulan Grey, ia hanya butuh tiga langkah untuk sampai ke guanya, dan ketika memandang sekeliling ia tidak melihat apa pun di dalamnya.
claims.quote: She only made three strides before she had reached her cave, and when she looked about, she could see nothing in it

claims.statement: Hatupatu repeats his charm "O rock open for me, open"; the rock opened and he hid himself in it, and the woman looked and could not find him.
claims.statement_id: Hatupatu mengucapkan mantra "O rock open for me, open"; batu itu terbuka dan ia bersembunyi di dalamnya, dan sang perempuan melihat tetapi tidak dapat menemukannya.
claims.quote: and she almost caught Hatupatu ; and he thought, I'm done for now. ... O rock open for me, open.' Then the rock opened, and he hid himself in it, and the woman looked and could not find him

claims.statement: A pet bird that escaped flew away to fetch back the woman they all belonged to, whose name was Kurangaituku.
claims.statement_id: Seekor burung peliharaan yang lolos terbang untuk menjemput perempuan pemiliknya, yang bernama Kurangaituku.
claims.quote: it flew away to fetch back the woman they all belonged to. Her name was Kuran- gaituku.

claims.statement: The Minka or Minka Bird is an owl-like bird in Ngarrindjeri stories along the Murray River.
claims.statement_id: Minka atau Minka Bird adalah burung yang digambarkan sebagai burung hantu dalam kisah suku Ngarrindjeri di Murray River, South Australia.
claims.quote: The Minka or Minka Bird is a bird, sometimes described as an owl, that featured in the stories of the Ngarrindjeri people of the Murray River in South Australia.

claims.statement: The Minka foretold death, whereas the similar mulduwanke stole children.
claims.statement_id: Burung Minka meramalkan kematian, berbeda dengan mulduwanke yang menculik anak-anak.
claims.quote: The mulduwanke is a similar owl or bird of the Ngarrindjeri, but instead of foretelling death it stole children.

claims.statement: Both were believed to live in dark recesses.
claims.statement_id: Keduanya diyakini tinggal di ceruk-ceruk gelap.
claims.quote: Both were believed to live in dark recesses.
