claims.statement: The Muldjewangk or Mulyawonk is a water creature in Ngarrindjeri mythology inhabiting the Murray River.
claims.statement_id: Muldjewangk atau Mulyawonk adalah makhluk air dalam mitologi Ngarrindjeri yang mendiami Murray River dan Lake Alexandrina.
claims.quote: The Muldjewangk or Mulyawonk is a water-creature in Ngarrindjeri mythology that inhabited the Murray River, particularly Lake Alexandrina.

claims.statement: It was used as a deterrent for Aboriginal children wishing to play near the riverside after dark.
claims.statement_id: Kisah makhluk ini digunakan untuk mencegah anak-anak bermain di tepi sungai setelah gelap.
claims.quote: It was used as a deterrent for Aboriginal children who wished to play near the riverside after dark.

claims.statement: A legend tells of a Muldjewangk attacking a steamboat with two great hands grasping the hull.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah legenda mengisahkan Muldjewangk menyerang kapal uap dengan dua tangan besar mencengkeram lambung kapal.
claims.quote: One legend tells of a Muldjewangk who attacked a steamboat owned by European settlers. The captain saw two great hands grasping the hull of the boat so he grabbed his gun.

claims.statement: The captain broke out in weeping red blisters over his body and took six months to die.
claims.statement_id: Kapten kapal tersebut kemudian menderita lepuh merah di sekujur tubuhnya dan meninggal dalam enam bulan.
claims.quote: Soon after, the captain broke out in weeping red blisters over his body, and took six months to die.

claims.statement: Large clumps of floating seaweed are said to hide Muldjewangks and are to be avoided.
claims.statement_id: Rumpun rumput laut terapung yang besar konon menyembunyikan Muldjewangk dan harus dihindari.
claims.quote: Large clumps of floating seaweed  are said to hide Muldjewangks and are to be avoided.

claims.statement: According to Warki/Ramindjeri Elders, the Lakalinyeri (language groups or clans) grouped together as the Ngarrindjeri people share a story of a water spirit known as the Mulyawonk; Australians may also know this mythical being as a "bunyip".
claims.statement_id: Menurut tetua Warki/Ramindjeri, Lakalinyeri (kelompok bahasa atau klan) yang dikelompokkan sebagai bangsa Ngarrindjeri berbagi kisah tentang roh air bernama Mulyawonk; orang Australia juga mungkin mengenal makhluk mitos ini sebagai "bunyip".
claims.quote: Warki/ Ramindjeri Elders Nita McAdam and Collin Koolmatrie ... the Lakalinyeri (language groups or clans) that are grouped together as the Ngarrindjeri people share a story of a water spirit known as the Mulyawonk. Australians may also know this mythical being as a "bunyip".

claims.statement: The story is about a Ngarrindjeri Ko:ni (man) who was greedy catching more fish than he needed; the Elders were so angry that as a punishment they turned him into the Mulyawonk, a half fish, half man creature, and banished him to the deep water forever.
claims.statement_id: Kisah itu tentang seorang laki-laki Ngarrindjeri (Ko:ni) yang serakah menangkap ikan lebih dari yang ia perlukan; para tetua sangat marah dan sebagai hukuman mengubahnya menjadi Mulyawonk, makhluk setengah ikan setengah manusia, dan mengasingkannya ke air dalam selamanya.
claims.quote: about a Ngarrindjeri Ko:ni (man) who was greedy catching more fish than he needed. ... The Elders were so angry with this man that as a punishment they turned him into the Mulyawonk - a half fish, half man creature and banished him to the deep water forever.

claims.statement: At a later time a child swimming in the water disappeared and the terrified father searched for his child; diving deep he found the Mulyawonk lair and the child, who was rescued and brought safely back to the shore.
claims.statement_id: Kemudian seorang anak yang berenang menghilang dan sang ayah yang ketakutan mencarinya; dengan menyelam dalam ia menemukan sarang Mulyawonk dan anak itu, yang diselamatkan dan dibawa kembali ke tepi dengan selamat.
claims.quote: However, at a later time a child swimming in the water disappeared and the terrified Father frantically searched for his child. Diving deep under the water he found the Mulyawonk lair and the child, who was rescued and brought safely back to the shore.

claims.statement: Ngarrindjeri children are told never to swim alone or to take more fish than they can eat from the rivers and swamps; the story teaches children water safety and respect for the fishes of the rivers, lakes and swamps.
claims.statement_id: Anak-anak Ngarrindjeri diberi tahu agar tidak berenang sendirian atau mengambil ikan lebih dari yang bisa mereka makan dari sungai dan rawa; kisah ini mengajarkan keselamatan di air dan rasa hormat terhadap ikan di sungai, danau, dan rawa.
claims.quote: Ngarrindjeri children are told never to swim alone or to take more fish than they can eat from the rivers and swamps. This story teaches children water safety and respect for the fishes of the rivers, lakes and swamps.

claims.statement: Nanaue is a demigod from Hawaiian mythology who can shapeshift into a giant shark.
claims.statement_id: Nanaue adalah manusia setengah dewa dalam mitologi Hawaiian yang memiliki mulut hiu di punggung dan mampu berubah wujud menjadi hiu raksasa.
claims.quote: Nanaue is a demigod from Hawaiian mythology. He is described as a man with the mouth of a shark on his back who can shapeshift into a giant shark.

claims.statement: Nanaue is the son of Kāmohoaliʻi, king of sharks, born with a shark mouth on his back.
claims.statement_id: Nanaue adalah putra dari Kāmohoaliʻi raja hiu dan terlahir dengan mulut hiu di punggungnya.
claims.quote: Nanaue is the son of Kāmohoaliʻi, who is the king of sharks. He was born with a shark's mouth on his back.

claims.statement: He took up residence in Kaneana cave where he would leave human bodies before eating them.
claims.statement_id: Ia tinggal di Kaneana cave tempat dirinya menyimpan mayat manusia sebelum memakannya.
claims.quote: He took up residence in Kaneana cave where he would leave human bodies to rot before eating them, as he found rotted flesh to be tastiest.

claims.statement: When Nanaue worked, others took off his clothing, revealing his shark mouth on his back.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Nanaue bekerja, pekerja lain membuka pakaiannya dan menampakkan mulut hiu di punggungnya.
claims.quote: When Nanaue was a man, ʻUmi-a-Līloa, the king of Hawaii, issued an order for all men to till a large plantation for the king. When Nanaue worked, other workers took off his clothing, revealing his shark mouth on his back.

claims.statement: Nanaue escaped being burned alive by shapeshifting into a shark to swim away.
claims.statement_id: Nanaue melarikan diri dari hukuman mati dengan berdoa kepada ayahnya lalu berubah menjadi hiu untuk berenang pergi.
claims.quote: The King had Nanaue tied to a stake to be burned alive, but Nanaue prayed to his father and escaped, shapeshifting into a shark to swim away.

claims.statement: The people of Molokai prayed to the demigod Unauna, who burned Nanaue alive.
claims.statement_id: Masyarakat di Molokai berdoa kepada Unauna yang akhirnya membakar Nanaue hidup-hidup.
claims.quote: The people of Molokai prayed to the demigod Unauna, who burned Nanaue alive.

claims.statement: Nanaue is called the shark-man of Waipio in the time of Umi.
claims.statement_id: Nanaue disebut manusia hiu (shark-man) dari Waipio pada masa Umi.
claims.quote: Nanaue is the shark-man of Waipio in the time of Umi

claims.statement: When detected at Waipio he turns into a shark and swims to Hana, where he marries the sister of a petty chief; at Molokai he lives at Poniu-o-Hua.
claims.statement_id: Ketika ketahuan di Waipio ia berubah menjadi hiu dan berenang ke Hana, tempat ia menikahi saudari seorang kepala (chief) kecil; di Molokai ia tinggal di Poniu-o-Hua.
claims.quote: When detected at Waipio he turns into a shark and swims to Hana, where he marries the sister of a petty chief. At Molokai he lives at Poniu-o-Hua.

claims.statement: The marks of the struggle are to be seen on the Kainalu hillslope and on a grooved rock called Pu‘u-mano, around which the ropes holding the net that caught him were wound.
claims.statement_id: Tanda-tanda pergumulan dapat dilihat di lereng bukit Kainalu dan pada batu beralur bernama Pu‘u-mano, tempat tali jaring yang menahannya dililitkan.
claims.quote: and the marks of the struggle are to be seen on the Kainalu hillslope and on a grooved rock called Pu‘u-mano about which the ropes were wound which held the net with which he was caught.

claims.statement: In the mythology of Tahiti, Pua Tu Tahi was one of the giant monster clams of the deep in the legend of Rata.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Tahiti, Pua Tu Tahi adalah salah satu kerang monster raksasa di laut dalam dalam legenda Rata.
claims.quote: In the mythology of Tahiti, Pua Tu Tahi was one of the giant monster clams of the deep in the legend of Rata.

claims.statement: In the Tahitian version, Rata is born after Tumu-nui, his four rat brothers and his brother-in-law Vahieroa, Rata's father, have all been swallowed by a giant clam while voyaging to Tu-i-hiti.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Tahiti, Rata lahir setelah Tumu-nui, empat saudara tikusnya, dan iparnya Vahieroa (ayah Rata) semuanya ditelan seekor kerang raksasa ketika berlayar menuju Tu-i-hiti.
claims.quote: Rata is son of Vahieroa and Maemae-a-rohi, sister of the ruling chief of North Tahiti, Tumu-nui. ... He is born after Tumu-nui and his four rat brothers ... and his brother-in-law Vahieroa, father of Rata, have all been swallowed by a giant clam while voyaging to Tu-i-hiti

claims.statement: The warriors who accompany Rata slay all the monsters; first they slay the great clam, then recover the bones of the dead and also Rata's living mother.
claims.statement_id: Para pejuang yang menyertai Rata membunuh semua monster di jalan mereka; yang pertama dibunuh adalah kerang raksasa, lalu mereka mengambil kembali tulang orang-orang yang tewas dan juga ibu Rata yang masih hidup.
claims.quote: accompany him, and slay all the monsters ... First they slay the great clam, recover the bones of the dead, and also Rata’s living mother

claims.statement: In Tahitian mythology, Rata's uncle, king Tumu-nui, and his father Vahieroa are swallowed by a great clam, Pua Tu Tahi, on their way to Pitcairn.
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitologi Tahiti, paman Rata, raja Tumu-nui, dan ayahnya Vahieroa ditelan kerang besar bernama Pua Tu Tahi dalam perjalanan ke Pitcairn.
claims.quote: Rata, in Tahitian mythology, is said to have become king of Tahiti when his uncle, king Tumu-nui, and his father Vahieroa are swallowed by a great clam, Pua Tu Tahi, while they are on their way to Pitcairn.

claims.statement: En route for Pitcairn, Rata and his crew are sucked down into the same clam but cut the monster open with their spears, rescue the remains of Rata's father and uncle, and bury them in Tahiti.
claims.statement_id: Dalam perjalanan ke Pitcairn, Rata dan awak kapalnya terisap ke dalam kerang yang sama, tetapi mereka membelah monster itu dengan tombak, menyelamatkan sisa jasad ayah dan paman Rata, dan menguburkannya di Tahiti.
claims.quote: While en route for Pitcairn, Rata and his crew are sucked down into the same clam, but they use their spears to cut the monster open. They rescue the remains of Rata's father and uncle and bury them back in Tahiti.

claims.statement: In the tale, one figure invokes monsters who guard the way to let him pass but to attack Tumu-nui should he attempt to follow.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, seorang tokoh memanggil monster-monster penjaga jalan agar membiarkannya lewat tetapi menyerang Tumu-nui bila ia mencoba mengikuti.
claims.quote: He invokes monsters who guard the way to let him pass but to attack Tumu-nui should he attempt to follow.

claims.statement: In Mangaian mythology, Tamangori is a legendary giant.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Mangaian, Tamangori adalah raksasa legendaris.
claims.quote: In Mangaian mythology, Tamangori is a legendary giant.

claims.statement: Tamangori is described as over nine feet in height, moving silently and eating humans.
claims.statement_id: Tamangori tingginya lebih dari sembilan kaki, berambut hitam disanggul, mampu bergerak tanpa suara dan memakan manusia.
claims.quote: Tamangori is described as over nine feet in height, with long black hair tied in a traditional bun. He could move silently and ate humans.

claims.statement: He was killed by two brothers, Pa and Pe, from a village called Ivirua.
claims.statement_id: Ia dibunuh oleh dua bersaudara, Pa dan Pe, dari desa bernama Ivirua.
claims.quote: He was killed by two brothers, Pa and Pe, from a village called Ivirua.

claims.statement: In the mythology of Mangaia in the Cook Islands, the Tapairu are elves or fairies named after daughters of Miru.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Mangaia di Cook Islands, Tapairu adalah peri yang dinamai menurut empat putri Miru dari alam bawah.
claims.quote: In the mythology of Mangaia in the Cook Islands, the Tapairu are elves or fairies, who are named after the four daughters of Miru, the deformed goddess of the underworld.

claims.statement: They were said to have been present when mortals danced in honor of their brother, Tau-Titi.
claims.statement_id: Mereka konon hadir ketika manusia menari untuk menghormati saudara mereka Tau-Titi.
claims.quote: They were said to have been present when mortals danced in honor of their brother, Tau-Titi.

claims.statement: They were also associated with the god Tane.
claims.statement_id: Mereka juga dikaitkan dengan dewa Tane.
claims.quote: They were also associated with the god Tane.

claims.statement: The deformed and ugly Miru has her home in the nether-world, where she cooks human spirits in her oven.
claims.statement_id: Miru yang cacat dan buruk rupa tinggal di dunia bawah, tempat ia memasak roh manusia di tungkunya.
claims.quote: The deformed and ugly Miru has her home in the nether-world, where she cooks human spirits in her oven.

claims.statement: Besides Tautiti, the pitiless spirit-eater has four daughters, called Tapairu, or peerless ones, on account of their matchless beauty.
claims.statement_id: Selain Tautiti, Miru si pemakan roh yang tak berbelas kasih memiliki empat putri bernama Tapairu, atau "yang tiada tara", karena kecantikan mereka yang tiada bandingnya.
claims.quote: Besides Tautiti, the pitiless spirit-eater has four daughters, called Tapairu, or peerless ones, on account of their matchless beauty.

claims.statement: These fairies, always associated with the worship of Tane, would take part in the dance provided that one end of the dancing ground were well covered with fresh cut banana leaves.
claims.statement_id: Peri-peri ini selalu dikaitkan dengan pemujaan Tane dan mau ikut menari asalkan salah satu ujung tempat menari dialasi daun pisang segar.
claims.quote: These fairies, always associated with the worship of Tane, would even deign to take part in the dance, provided that one end of the dancing ground were well covered with fresh cut banana leaves.

claims.statement: As soon as the morning star rose they disappeared and returned to their gloomy home in Avaiki.
claims.statement_id: Begitu bintang fajar terbit, mereka menghilang dan kembali ke kediaman mereka yang muram di Avaiki.
claims.quote: As soon as the morning star rose they disappeared, and returned to their gloomy home in Avaiki.

claims.statement: The tale of Tiddalik the frog is a creation story from Australian Indigenous Dreaming Stories.
claims.statement_id: Kisah katak Tiddalik adalah kisah penciptaan dari kisah Dreaming penduduk pribumi Australia.
claims.quote: The tale of Tiddalik the frog is a creation story from Australian Indigenous Dreaming Stories.

claims.statement: In some Aboriginal language groups, Tiddalik is known as Molok.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa kelompok bahasa Aborigin, Tiddalik dikenal sebagai Molok.
claims.quote: In some Aboriginal language groups, Tiddalik is known as "Molok".

claims.statement: In the creation myth, Tiddalik awoke in Wollombi Valley and drank all available fresh water.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos penciptaan, Tiddalik terbangun di Wollombi Valley dengan rasa haus dan menelan seluruh air tawar.
claims.quote: In the creation myth, Tiddalik awoke one morning in Wollombi Valley with an insatiable thirst and started to drink until he had gulped down all the available fresh water.

claims.statement: Creatures and plant life everywhere began to die due to lack of moisture.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk hidup dan tumbuhan mulai mati karena kekurangan air.
claims.quote: Creatures and plant life everywhere began to die due to lack of moisture.

claims.statement: Nabunum the eel made Tiddalik laugh when he tied himself in comical shapes.
claims.statement_id: Belut Nabunum membuat Tiddalik tertawa saat meliukkan tubuhnya dalam bentuk-bentuk lucu.
claims.quote: This was successfully coordinated by a wise old owl, when Nabunum the eel made Tiddalik laugh when he tied himself in comical shapes.

claims.statement: As Tiddalik laughed, the water rushed out to replenish lakes, swamps and rivers.
claims.statement_id: Saat Tiddalik tertawa, air memancar keluar mengisi kembali danau, rawa, dan sungai.
claims.quote: As Tiddalik laughed, the water rushed out of him to replenish the lakes, swamps and rivers.

claims.statement: According to the article's author, the story originally belonged to the Aboriginal people of South Gippsland, in Victoria.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis artikel, kisah ini semula milik masyarakat Aborigin South Gippsland di Victoria.
claims.quote: Actually, the story originally belonged to the Aboriginal people of South Gippsland, in Victoria

claims.statement: Every version of Tiddalik now circulating can be traced back to early records that locate the story on the coast of South Gippsland near Port Albert.
claims.statement_id: Semua versi Tiddalik yang beredar sekarang dapat ditelusuri ke catatan-catatan awal yang menempatkan kisah itu di wilayah pesisir South Gippsland dekat Port Albert.
claims.quote: Each of the myriad versions of Tiddalik which now abound across the globe can be traced back to these early records, which locate the story in the coastal area of South Gippsland near Port Albert

claims.statement: The missionary John Bulmer, the pastoralist Edward Curr, and the geologists Alfred Howitt and Robert Brough Smyth all recorded early versions of the Tiddalik story.
claims.statement_id: Misionaris John Bulmer, peternak Edward Curr, serta ahli geologi Alfred Howitt dan Robert Brough Smyth semuanya mencatat versi awal kisah Tiddalik.
claims.quote: Among those anthropologists were the missionary John Bulmer, the pastoralist Edward Curr, and the geologists Alfred Howitt and Robert Brough Smyth, all of whom recorded early versions of the Tiddalik story.

claims.statement: In the original Kurnai versions recorded in the nineteenth century, Tiddalik's release of water was a natural disaster, causing many to drown and many to become stranded on islands.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi asli Kurnai yang dicatat pada abad ke-19, pelepasan air oleh Tiddalik adalah bencana alam yang membuat banyak orang tenggelam dan banyak lainnya terdampar di pulau-pulau.
claims.quote: In fact, in the original Kurnai versions recorded in the nineteenth century, Tiddalik's release of water into the environment was a natural disaster, causing many to drown and many to become stranded on the islands

claims.statement: Those who were stranded were rescued by Borun the pelican, whose feathers were then entirely black.
claims.statement_id: Mereka yang terdampar diselamatkan oleh Borun si pelikan, yang saat itu bulunya hitam seluruhnya.
claims.quote: Those who were stranded were rescued by Borun the pelican, whose feathers were then entirely black.

claims.statement: The problem is that the Water-holding Frog is not found in or anywhere near Tiddalik's original home in Gippsland.
claims.statement_id: Masalahnya, katak penyimpan air tidak ditemukan di Gippsland atau di dekat tempat asal Tiddalik.
claims.quote: The problem is that the Water-holding Frog is not found in or anywhere near Tiddalik's original home in Gippsland.

claims.statement: The author says that for children as well as adults it is a story with a moral lesson about greed and about how it is better to share.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis, bagi anak-anak maupun orang dewasa ini adalah kisah dengan pelajaran moral tentang keserakahan dan tentang lebih baiknya berbagi.
claims.quote: For children, as well as adults, it is a story with a moral lesson about greed and about how it is better to share

claims.statement: In the mythology of Mangaia in the Cook Islands, Tikokura is a sea-dwelling evil spirit in the shape of a storm wave.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Mangaia di Cook Islands, Tikokura adalah roh jahat penghuni laut dalam bentuk gelombang badai.
claims.quote: In the mythology of Mangaia in the Cook Islands, Tikokura is a sea-dwelling evil spirit in the shape of a storm wave.

claims.statement: Ngaru determined to try his strength against Tikokura and his shark-like companion, Tumuitearetoka.
claims.statement_id: Ngaru memutuskan untuk menguji kekuatannya melawan Tikokura dan rekannya yang mirip hiu bernama Tumuitearetoka.
claims.quote: Ngaru determined to try his strength against Tikokura and his shark-like companion, Tumuitearetoka.

claims.statement: He provided himself with a surfboard named Orua (the two).
claims.statement_id: Ngaru membekali dirinya dengan papan selancar bernama Orua.
claims.quote: He provided himself with a surfboard named Orua (the two).

claims.statement: After eight days and nights, Ngaru threw his surfboard to the monsters, who retired to the deep.
claims.statement_id: Setelah delapan hari delapan malam, Ngaru melemparkan papan selancarnya dan monster-monster itu kembali ke kediaman mereka di laut dalam.
claims.quote: After eight days and nights, Ngaru threw his surfboard to the monsters, who gladly retired to their home in the deep, while Ngaru went off to find Tongatea, his wife (Gill 1876:225-227).

claims.statement: Thirsting for distinction, Ngaru resolved to try his strength against some of the numerous monsters and evil spirits of his time.
claims.statement_id: Haus akan kemasyhuran, Ngaru bertekad menguji kekuatannya melawan sejumlah monster dan roh jahat pada zamannya.
claims.quote: Thirsting for distinction, Ngaru resolved to try his strength against some of the numerous monsters and evil spirits of his time.

claims.statement: Tumuitearetoka is described as a vast shark that fed exclusively on human flesh, and these evil spirits always went in each other's company.
claims.statement_id: Tumuitearetoka digambarkan sebagai hiu raksasa yang hanya memakan daging manusia, dan roh-roh jahat itu selalu pergi bersama.
claims.quote: or a vast shark, which fed exclusively upon human flesh. These evil spirits always went in each other's company

claims.statement: Moko sat on a projecting crag of rock to watch over his grandson, who advanced to the outer edge of the reef where the surf ceaselessly beats and loudly cursed the sea-monsters by name.
claims.statement_id: Moko duduk di tonjolan karang untuk menjaga keselamatan cucunya, yang maju ke tepi luar terumbu tempat ombak tak henti memukul dan dengan lantang mengutuk para monster laut itu dengan menyebut nama mereka.
claims.quote: Moko sat on a projecting crag of rock to watch over the safety of his grandson, who now advanced to the outer edge of the reef, where the surf ceaselessly beats, and loudly cursed these sea-monsters by name.

claims.statement: For eight weary days and nights the contest went on, until the exhausted Ngaru ended it by throwing his surf-board to the sea-monsters, who gladly retired to their ancient haunts in the deep blue ocean.
claims.statement_id: Pertarungan itu berlangsung delapan hari delapan malam, sampai Ngaru yang kelelahan mengakhirinya dengan melemparkan papan selancarnya kepada para monster laut, yang dengan senang hati kembali ke tempat lama mereka di samudra biru yang dalam.
claims.quote: For eight weary days and nights this terrible contest went on, until the exhausted Ngaru put an end to it by throwing his surf-board to the sea-monsters, who gladly retired to their ancient haunts in the deep blue ocean.

claims.statement: Wirnpa is a rainmaking snake who according to Western Desert legend created the land around Percival Lakes in the Dreaming and repelled outsiders.
claims.statement_id: Wirnpa adalah ular pencipta hujan yang menciptakan tanah di sekitar Percival Lakes pada masa Dreaming dan gambarnya dipakai untuk menangkal orang luar.
claims.quote: Wirnpa is a rainmaking snake who according to Western Desert Australian Aboriginal legend created the land around the Percival Lakes in Wirnpa country, Australia in the Dreaming and whose image was used to repel outsiders.

claims.statement: Before they became snakes, the jila ancestral beings were men who made rain, shaped the features of the land and introduced practices of law into the jila Country.
claims.statement_id: Sebelum menjadi ular, para leluhur jila adalah manusia yang membuat hujan, membentuk bentang alam, dan memperkenalkan hukum ke wilayah jila.
claims.quote: Before they became snakes, however, these ancestral beings were men who made rain, shaped the features of the land and introduced practices of law into the jila Country.

claims.statement: Wirnpa was one of the most powerful of the jila men and the last to travel the desert before becoming a snake and entering the spring that bears his name; his adventures are celebrated in the songs and stories of many language groups.
claims.statement_id: Wirnpa adalah salah satu laki-laki jila yang paling kuat dan yang terakhir menjelajahi gurun sebelum menjadi ular dan masuk ke mata air yang memakai namanya; petualangannya dirayakan dalam lagu dan kisah banyak kelompok bahasa.
claims.quote: Wirnpa was one of the most powerful of the jila men and the last to travel the desert before becoming a snake and entering the spring, which bears his name. His adventures are celebrated in the songs and stories of many language groups.

claims.statement: Aboriginal people enter Wirnpa, which lies west of the stock route, ritually, sweeping the ground with branches and approaching in single file.
claims.statement_id: Orang Aborigin memasuki Wirnpa, yang terletak di barat jalur ternak, secara ritual: menyapu tanah dengan dahan dan mendekat dalam satu barisan.
claims.quote: Aboriginal people enter Wirnpa, which lies west of the stock route, ritually, sweeping the ground with branches and approaching in single file.

claims.statement: On either side of the stock route, jila such as Kurtal and Wirnpa live on at these sites; their enduring power and importance is asserted in the songs, ceremonies and paintings of their people.
claims.statement_id: Di kedua sisi jalur ternak, jila seperti Kurtal dan Wirnpa tetap hidup di situs-situs itu; kekuatan dan arti pentingnya ditegaskan dalam lagu, upacara, dan lukisan umat mereka.
claims.quote: Either side of the stock route, jila such as Kurtal and Wirnpa live on at these sites. Their enduring power and importance is asserted in the songs, ceremonies and paintings of their people.

claims.statement: The museum notes that many of these people worry about proposals to mine the Country around Wirnpa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam keterangan museum, banyak orang dari kelompok-kelompok itu khawatir terhadap usulan menambang wilayah di sekitar Wirnpa.
claims.quote: Today, many of these people worry about proposals to mine the Country around Wirnpa.

claims.statement: Agunua is the cosmic serpent god of San Cristobal Island and chief god of whom all others are aspects.
claims.statement_id: Agunua atau Hatuibwari adalah dewa ular kosmis tertinggi masyarakat Makira di Solomon Islands di mana dewa lain merupakan aspek dirinya.
claims.quote: Agunua (alternate name Hatuibwari) is the cosmic serpent god of the people of San Cristobal Island (now better known as Makira) of the Solomon Islands, He is the chief god, and all other gods are only an aspect of him.

claims.statement: The first coconut from each tree is sacred to Agunua.
claims.statement_id: Buah kelapa pertama dari setiap pohon dikeramatkan untuk Agunua.
claims.quote: The first coconut from each tree is sacred to Agunua.

claims.statement: He is also the god of the sea.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga merupakan dewa laut.
claims.quote: He is also the god of the sea.

claims.statement: He is worshiped through prayer, with many requesting good health and rich harvests.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipuja lewat doa di mana orang-orang memohon kesehatan yang baik serta hasil panen melimpah.
claims.quote: He is worshiped through prayer, with many requesting general good health and rich harvests of him.

claims.statement: There is one figona who seems almost like a supreme spirit, called Agunua.
claims.statement_id: Ada satu figona yang tampak hampir seperti roh tertinggi, bernama Agunua.
claims.quote: There is one, indeed, who seems almost like a supreme spirit, called Agunua.

claims.statement: Agunua is a name for Hatuibwari, the winged serpent.
claims.statement_id: Agunua adalah nama untuk Hatuibwari, ular bersayap.
claims.quote: Agunua is a name for Hatuibwari, the winged serpent.

claims.statement: In the account of the men of Ngorangora, Agunua created all things: the sea, the land, men and animals, thunder, lightning, rain and storms.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penuturan para lelaki Ngorangora, Agunua menciptakan segala sesuatu: laut, daratan, manusia, hewan, guntur, kilat, hujan, dan badai.
claims.quote: Agunua created all things—the sea, the land, men, and animals, thunder, lightning, rain, and storms

claims.statement: Almost all of these local figona are represented as female snakes, Agunua as a male snake.
claims.statement_id: Hampir semua figona setempat digambarkan sebagai ular betina, sedangkan Agunua sebagai ular jantan.
claims.quote: Almost all of these local figona are represented as female snakes, Agunua as a male snake.

claims.statement: The first drinking nut from a coco-nut tree is sacred to Agunua, and its milk is poured out as a libation in the sacred grove.
claims.statement_id: Buah kelapa minum pertama dari sebatang pohon kelapa dikeramatkan bagi Agunua, dan airnya dituangkan sebagai persembahan di hutan keramat.
claims.quote: The first drinking nut from a coco-nut tree is sacred to Agunua, and the milk is poured out as a libation in the sacred grove.

claims.statement: It is told that Agunua was thirsty and rain fell to assuage his thirst; this was the origin of rain.
claims.statement_id: Dikisahkan Agunua haus lalu hujan turun untuk meredakan hausnya; itulah asal mula hujan.
claims.quote: He was thirsty and rain fell to assuage his thirst. This was the origin of rain.

claims.statement: The centre of the cult of Agunua is at Haununu, on the south-west coast.
claims.statement_id: Pusat pemujaan Agunua berada di Haununu, di pesisir barat daya.
claims.quote: The centre of the cult is at Haununu, on the south-west coast

claims.statement: In dreamtime mythology, the Arkaroo is a serpent who drank all the waters of Lake Frome in South Australia.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa dreamtime, Arkaroo adalah ular yang meminum semua air di Lake Frome di South Australia.
claims.quote: In the dreamtime of Australian Aboriginal mythology, the Arkaroo is a serpent who drank all the waters of Lake Frome in South Australia, the latter remaining a large salt pan most of the time.

claims.statement: The Arkaroo retracted into the mountains, carving the valleys of the Gammon Ranges in the northern Flinders Ranges.
claims.statement_id: Arkaroo beristirahat ke pegunungan barat dan tubuhnya mengukir lembah-lembah Gammon Ranges di Flinders Ranges utara.
claims.quote: Heavily filled and tired, the Arkaroo retracted for a nap into the mountains west, carving by his body the valleys of what is known today as the Gammon Ranges in the northern Flinders Ranges.

claims.statement: Attacked by mystic beasts, water from his rests formed waterholes such as Arkaroola Springs.
claims.statement_id: Ia diserang makhluk mistis lain dan air yang keluar dari tempat istirahatnya menghasilkan mata air seperti Arkaroola Springs.
claims.quote: He was attacked by other mystic beasts and let water on his rests, each position resulting in a waterhole, such as that of Arkaroola Springs and others.

claims.statement: Rumblings of the Arkaroo can be heard in the mountains, explained by seismic activity.
claims.statement_id: Gemuruh Arkaroo masih terdengar di pegunungan yang dijelaskan secara ilmiah oleh aktivitas seismik.
claims.quote: Today as in ancient times, rumblings of the Arkaroo can be heard in the mountains, which are scientifically explained by the seismic activity of the ranges.

claims.statement: The Arkaroo gave origin to place names including Arkaroola Village, Arkaroola Creek, and Arkaroo Rock in Wilpena Pound.
claims.statement_id: Arkaroo menjadi asal-usul nama tempat seperti Arkaroola Village, Arkaroola Creek, Arkaroola Springs dan Arkaroo Rock di Wilpena Pound.
claims.quote: The Arkaroo has given origin of name to places in this region, namely Arkaroola Village, Arkaroola Creek, Arkaroola Springs and the Arkaroo Rock in Wilpena Pound.

claims.statement: Arkaroo was a great serpent from the Dreamtime who lived in the Gammon Ranges south of Arkaroola.
claims.statement_id: Arkaroo adalah ular besar dari Dreamtime yang tinggal di Gammon Ranges, di selatan Arkaroola.
claims.quote: Arkaroo was a great serpent from the Dreamtime who lived in the Gammon Ranges south of Arkaroola.

claims.statement: According to Adnyamathanha stories, Arkaroo grew very thirsty, slithered down to the plains and drank Lake Frome and Lake Callabonna dry.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah masyarakat Adnyamathanha, Arkaroo sangat haus lalu turun ke dataran dan menghabiskan air Lake Frome dan Lake Callabonna.
claims.quote: According to the stories about him among the Adnyamathanha people, he felt very thirsty so slithered down to the plains and drank Lake Frome and Lake Callabonna dry.

claims.statement: The large volume of salty water he drank gave him a terrible bellyache, which the Aboriginal people believed caused the rumblings from beneath the ground in the Gammon Ranges.
claims.statement_id: Air asin dalam jumlah besar yang ia minum membuat perutnya sakit hebat; masyarakat Aborigin percaya itulah penyebab gemuruh dari bawah tanah di Gammon Ranges.
claims.quote: The large volume of salty water he drank gave him a terrible bellyache. The Aboriginal People believed that was the cause of the rumblings coming from beneath the ground in the Gammon Ranges

claims.statement: An alternative explanation is that the sounds result from minor tremors along fault lines produced by earth movements associated with readjustment of the crust after uplift of the area.
claims.statement_id: Penjelasan alternatif menyebut bunyi itu berasal dari getaran kecil di sepanjang garis sesar akibat pergerakan bumi terkait penyesuaian kerak setelah wilayah itu terangkat.
claims.quote: An alternative explanation is that the sounds result from minor tremors along fault lines produced by earth movements associated with readjustment of the crust after uplift of the area.

claims.statement: Paralana Hot Springs is described as one of the most important of the waterholes left by Arkaroo.
claims.statement_id: Paralana Hot Springs disebut sebagai salah satu lubang air terpenting yang ditinggalkan Arkaroo.
claims.quote: Paralana Hot Springs is one of the most important of the waterholes left by Arkaroo.

claims.statement: Bamapama (Ure) is a trickster god in Aboriginal mythology.
claims.statement_id: Bamapama (Ure) adalah dewa penipu dalam mitologi Aborygenów.
claims.quote: Bamapama (Ure) – bóg oszust w mitologii Aborygenów.

claims.statement: In Yolngu mythology, Bamapana is a trickster god who causes discord.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Yolngu, Bamapana adalah dewa penipu yang menyebabkan perselisihan.
claims.quote: In Yolngu mythology, Bamapana is a trickster god who causes discord.

claims.statement: He broke a strict taboo in tribal tradition.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering melanggar tabu ketat masyarakat adat.
claims.quote: He is obscene and profane and once committed incest, thus breaking a strict taboo.

claims.statement: Bamapana is the trickster hero of the Murngin in northern Australia, "a crazy man".
claims.statement_id: Bamapana adalah pahlawan penipu (trickster) kelompok Murngin di Australia utara, "orang gila" (a crazy man).

claims.statement: Chinny-kinik was a dreaded cannibal giant from Australian Aboriginal mythology who terrorized the Yenpulla plain in South Australia.
claims.statement_id: Chinny-kinik adalah raksasa kanibal mengerikan dari mitologi Australian Aboriginal yang meneror dataran Yenpulla di South Australia.
claims.quote: Chinny-kinik was a dreaded cannibal giant from Australian Aboriginal mythology said to have terrorised the Yenpulla plain east of the Murray River in South Australia.

claims.statement: Two of his uncles tracked him to a sinkhole in Pekarra and found the entrance to a vast cave.
claims.statement_id: Dua pamannya melacak jejaknya ke sinkhole di daerah Pekarra dan menemukan pintu masuk ke gua luas.
claims.quote: Two of his uncles, members of the local clan whose numbers had been decimated, tracked him to a sinkhole in an area called Pekarra and discovered the entrance to a vast cave.

claims.statement: With Chinny-kinik sheltering inside, they stacked firewood at the entrance and ignited it.
claims.statement_id: Saat Chinny-kinik berlindung di dalam gua, mereka menumpuk kayu bakar di mulut gua dan menyalakannya.
claims.quote: With Chinny-kinik sheltering inside from a cold wind, they stacked the entrance with bundles of firewood and set them alight.

claims.statement: The uncles added logs to the blaze to seal the cannibal giant's doom.
claims.statement_id: Paman-pamannya menambahkan batang kayu ke kobaran api untuk menutup pintu masuk dan mengakhiri hidup sang raksasa.
claims.quote: The uncles added logs to the blaze to block the entrance and seal the cannibal giant’s doom.

claims.statement: In 1921 Tom Bellchambers, a renowned South Australian naturalist and conservationist, recorded the Indigenous legend of Chinny-kinik, the dreaded cannibal giant of the Murraylands.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1921 Tom Bellchambers, naturalis dan konservasionis terkenal dari South Australia, mencatat legenda Pribumi tentang Chinny-kinik, raksasa kanibal yang ditakuti di Murraylands.
claims.quote: In 1921 renowned South Australian naturalist and conservationist, Tom Bellchambers, recorded the Indigenous legend of Chinny-kinik, the dreaded cannibal giant of the Murraylands.

claims.statement: Chinny-kinik roamed a vast mallee-covered plain east of the Murray River, catching and devouring anyone he met.
claims.statement_id: Chinny-kinik berkeliaran di dataran luas berhutan mallee di sebelah timur Murray River, menangkap dan melahap siapa pun yang ia temui.
claims.quote: Chinny-kinik roamed a vast mallee-covered plain to the east of the Murray River, catching and devouring anyone he encountered.

claims.statement: His ravenous reign continued until two of his uncles, members of the decimated local clan, tracked his enormous footprints to a sinkhole in an area called Pekarra.
claims.statement_id: Kekejamannya berlanjut tanpa henti sampai dua pamannya, anggota klan setempat yang jumlahnya sudah menyusut drastis, melacak jejak kakinya yang sangat besar ke sebuah lubang runtuhan di daerah bernama Pekarra.
claims.quote: His ravenous reign continued unabated until two of his uncles, members of the local clan whose numbers had been decimated, tracked his enormous footprints to a sinkhole in an area called Pekarra.

claims.statement: Chinny-kinik's mighty struggles shook the earth as smoke wafted through his lair.
claims.statement_id: Perjuangan dahsyat Chinny-kinik mengguncang bumi saat asap menyusup ke sarangnya.
claims.quote: Chinny-kinik’s mighty struggles shook the earth as smoke wafted through his lair.

claims.statement: Bellchambers was determined to find the legendary cave and narrowed its likely location to a fifty-kilometre stretch of the western Murray Mallee.
claims.statement_id: Bellchambers bertekad menemukan gua legendaris itu dan mempersempit lokasinya ke bentang lima puluh kilometer di Murray Mallee bagian barat.
claims.quote: Bellchambers was determined to track down the legendary cave and narrowed the likely location to a fifty kilometre stretch of the western Murray Mallee

claims.statement: The article's author notes that some Aboriginal speakers did not distinguish the sounds p and b, so the cave site may in fact be "Bakara" rather than "Pekarra".
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis artikel, sebagian penutur Aborigin tidak membedakan bunyi p dan b, sehingga lokasi gua mungkin sebenarnya "Bakara", bukan "Pekarra".
claims.quote: some Aboriginal speakers did not make a distinction between the sounds ‘p’ and ‘b’. Instead of ‘Pekarra’, the cave site may in fact be ‘Bakara’.

claims.statement: The Bakara Well Cave was not discovered until the early 1970s, by Wayne Goedecke.
claims.statement_id: Gua Bakara Well baru ditemukan oleh Wayne Goedecke pada awal 1970-an.
claims.quote: It wasn’t until the early 1970s that Wayne Goedecke discovered the Bakara Well Cave

claims.statement: The author argues that the low sinkhole and gully leading to the collapse entrance to the south align with the description in the legend.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penulis artikel, lubang runtuhan yang rendah dan parit yang mengarah ke pintu masuk di selatan sesuai dengan deskripsi dalam legenda.
claims.quote: The low sinkhole and gully leading to the collapse entrance to the south align with the description in the legend.

claims.statement: Garkain is a legendary creature in Australian Aboriginal mythology of Arnhem Land haunting the jungle of Magurlipun.
claims.statement_id: Garkain adalah makhluk legendaris di Arnhem Land, Northern Territory, berwujud manusia-roh penghuni hutan Magurlipun.
claims.quote: Garkain is a legendary creature in the Australian Aboriginal mythology of Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory. He is said to be a spirit-man that haunts a dense jungle called Magurlipun near the Liverpool River's mouth.

claims.statement: Garkain kills unwary travellers by smothering them with loose folds of skin on his arms and legs.
claims.statement_id: Garkain membunuh pengelana yang masuk ke wilayahnya dengan membekap mereka memakai lipatan kulit di lengan dan kakinya.
claims.quote: Should an unwary traveller enter his domain, Garkain kills them by smothering them with the loose folds of skin on his arms and legs.

claims.statement: He is a nocturnal hunter who sleeps during the day under a pile of leaves.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah pemburu nokturnal yang tidur di siang hari di dasar hutan di bawah tumpukan daun.
claims.quote: He is a nocturnal hunter and sleeps during the day on the jungle floor under a pile of leaves.

claims.statement: He is capable of walking and flying but lacks speech and eats prey raw.
claims.statement_id: Ia seukuran manusia, mampu berjalan dan terbang, namun tidak dapat berbicara dan memakan mangsa secara mentah.
claims.quote: He is similar in size to an Aboriginal man, and is capable of both walking and flying, but lacks the power of speech and does not know how to make fire or tools, thus forcing him to catch prey with his bare hands and eat it raw.

claims.statement: In 1957 the anthropologist Charles P. Mountford donated a eucalyptus bark painting of Garkain (1948 or 1949) from the Gunbalanya Aboriginal community in western Arnhem Land to the Art Gallery of South Australia in Adelaide.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1957 antropolog Charles P. Mountford menyumbangkan lukisan kulit kayu eukaliptus bergambar Garkain (1948 atau 1949) dari komunitas Aborigin Gunbalanya di Arnhem Land barat kepada Art Gallery of South Australia di Adelaide.
claims.quote: In 1957, anthropologist Charles P. Mountford donated a eucalyptus bark painting of Garkain (1948 or 1949) from the Gunbalanya Aboriginal community in western Arnhem Land to the Art Gallery of South Australia in Adelaide.

claims.statement: The painting shows the creature's flaps of skin, and his feet are illustrated as footprints, as is common in depictions of spiritual and human beings.
claims.statement_id: Lukisan itu memperlihatkan lipatan kulit makhluk tersebut, dan kakinya digambarkan sebagai jejak kaki, seperti lazim pada penggambaran makhluk roh dan manusia.
claims.quote: The painting shows the creature's flaps of skin, and his feet are illustrated as footprints, as is common in depictions of spiritual and human beings.

claims.statement: Mountford noted similarities between Garkain and Warraguk and observed that overall the creature was not as feared as other spirit beings of the area such as the Namarakain and the Nabudi.
claims.statement_id: Mountford mencatat kemiripan antara Garkain dan Warraguk, serta mengamati bahwa secara keseluruhan makhluk ini tidak seditakuti makhluk roh lain di daerah itu seperti Namarakain dan Nabudi.
claims.quote: Mountford noted similarities between Garkain and Warraguk, and observed that the creature was overall not as feared as other spirit beings of the area like the Namarakain and the Nabudi.

claims.statement: The Art Gallery of South Australia's collection records a work titled Garkain by an unknown maker, from Gunbalanya (Oenpelli), western Arnhem Land, 1948 or 1949, in natural ochres on eucalyptus bark, a gift of Charles P. Mountford in 1957.
claims.statement_id: Koleksi Art Gallery of South Australia mencatat sebuah karya berjudul Garkain, tanpa pembuat yang diketahui, dari Gunbalanya (Oenpelli), Arnhem Land barat, 1948 atau 1949, dari ochre alami di atas kulit kayu eukaliptus, hadiah Charles P. Mountford 1957.
claims.quote: Unknown, Garkain, 1948 or 1949, Gunbalanya (Oenpelli), western Arnhem Land, Northern Territory, natural ochres on eucalyptus bark, 78.5 x 30.5 cm (irreg); Gift of Charles P. Mountford 1957

claims.statement: In Hawaiian mythology, Hauwahine was a moʻo and the guardian spirit of Kawainui Fishpond.
claims.statement_id: Hauwahine adalah sosok moʻo dan roh penjaga kolam ikan Kawainui serta kolam Pā'eo dan Kaʻelepulu.
claims.quote: In Hawaiian mythology, Hauwahine was a moʻo and the guardian spirit of Kawainui Fishpond as well as Pā'eo and Kaʻelepulu fishponds.

claims.statement: Hauwahine ensured food was available but removed fish if people were oppressed by the aliʻi.
claims.statement_id: Hauwahine memastikan ketersediaan makanan tetapi memindahkan ikan jika rakyat ditindas oleh aliʻi.
claims.quote: It was believed that Hauwahine ensured there was enough food available for the people, but removed the fish from the pond if the people living in the area were oppressed by the aliʻi.

claims.statement: In the Hawaiian language, the name Hauwahine literally means "female ruler".
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Hawaiian, nama Hauwahine secara harafiah berarti penguasa wanita.
claims.quote: In the Hawaiian language, the name Hauwahine literally means "female ruler".

claims.statement: She was believed to prevent sickness and pollution was considered an insult to her.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipercaya mencegah penyakit dan polusi dianggap sebagai penghinaan terhadapnya sehingga kolam dijaga kebersihannya.
claims.quote: She was additionally believed to prevent sickness. Pollution and overgrowth were thought to be insults to Hauwahine, which was one motivation for the Hawaiians to keep the fishpond clean.

claims.statement: Hau-wahine is the moʻo goddess of the ponds of Kawainui and Kaelepule in the Koolau district on Oahu; she brings abundant fish, punishes pond owners who oppress the poor, and wards off sickness.
claims.statement_id: Hau-wahine adalah dewi moʻo untuk kolam-kolam Kawainui dan Kaelepule di distrik Koolau, Oahu; ia mendatangkan ikan melimpah, menghukum pemilik kolam yang menindas orang miskin, dan menangkal penyakit.
claims.quote: Hau-wahine is the mo‘o goddess of the ponds of Kawainui and Kaelepule in Koolau district on Oahu. She brings abundance of fish, punishes the owners of the pond if they oppress the poor, and wards off sickness.

claims.statement: The goddess Hiʻiaka was believed to have fought all the moʻo except Hauwahine, for whom she chanted a mele.
claims.statement_id: Dewi Hiʻiaka dipercaya telah melawan semua moʻo kecuali Hauwahine, yang untuknya ia melantunkan sebuah mele.
claims.quote: The Hawaiian goddess Hiʻiaka was believed to have fought all the moʻo except for Hauwahine, for whom she chanted a mele.

claims.statement: Nā Pōhaku o Hauwahine, a basalt outcropping on the west side of Kawainui, was thought to be a favored location of Hauwahine; yellow grass and rushes were believed to mark her presence.
claims.statement_id: Nā Pōhaku o Hauwahine, singkapan basal di sisi barat Kawainui, dianggap sebagai tempat kesukaan Hauwahine; rumput kuning dan gelagah dipercaya menandai keberadaannya.
claims.quote: Nā Pōhaku o Hauwahine, a basalt outcropping on the west side of Kawainui, was thought to be a favored location of Hauwahine. Yellow grass and rushes were believed to mark her location.

claims.statement: In traditional stories of Southeastern Australia, Kinie Ger is an evil half-man, half-quoll beast.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah tradisional Southeastern Australia, Kinie Ger adalah binatang buas separuh manusia separuh quoll yang berburu memakai tombak.
claims.quote: In the traditional stories of Southeastern Australia, Kinie Ger is an evil half-man, half-quoll beast that hunts and kills the innocent with his spear, until he is himself killed in an ambush.

claims.statement: It had the head and body of a quoll but the limbs of a man.
claims.statement_id: Ia berkepala dan bertubuh quoll tetapi memiliki anggota badan manusia.
claims.quote: It was a ruthless killer with the head and body of a quoll but the limbs of a man.

claims.statement: The creature was killed by the owl and the crow who ambushed him at a water hole.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini dibunuh oleh burung hantu dan burung gagak yang menyergapnya di sumber air.
claims.quote: In the myth, the creature was stated to have been killed by the owl and the crow who ambushed him when he came to drink at a water hole.

claims.statement: When defeated, it shrank down and became the first quoll.
claims.statement_id: Saat dikalahkan, tubuhnya menyusut dan menjadi quoll pertama yang menurunkan seluruh bangsa quoll.
claims.quote: Supposedly when the creature was finally defeated, it shrank down and became the first quoll, the founding father of the quoll race.

claims.statement: From the early 1920s Unaipon studied Aboriginal mythology and compiled his versions of legends; Kinie Ger—The Native Cat was among the publications funded in 1928.
claims.statement_id: Sejak awal 1920-an Unaipon mempelajari mitologi Aborigin dan menyusun versi-versinya atas legenda; Kinie Ger—The Native Cat termasuk terbitan yang didanai pada 1928.
claims.quote: From the early 1920s Unaipon studied Aboriginal mythology and compiled his versions of legends; he was influenced by the classics and by his researches into Egyptology at the South Australian Museum. The A.F.A. funded publication of Hungarrda (1927), Kinie Ger—The Native Cat (1928) and Native Legends (1929).

claims.statement: In Aboriginal mythology, Kinie Ger was a ruthless and murderous beast with the head and body of a cat but the limbs of a man, who killed innocent people, animals and birds; he was killed by the owl and the crow who ambushed him as he came to drink at a water hole.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Aborigin, Kinie Ger adalah makhluk kejam dan haus darah berkepala dan bertubuh kucing tetapi berkaki tangan manusia, yang membunuh orang tak bersalah, hewan, dan burung; ia dibunuh oleh burung hantu dan burung gagak yang menyergapnya saat ia datang minum di lubang air.
claims.quote: In Australian Aborigine mythology, Kinie Ger was a ruthless and murderous beast with the head and body of a cat but the limbs of a man who went around killing innocent people, animals and birds. He was killed by the owl and the crow who ambushed him when he came to drink at a water hole.

claims.statement: Mungoon-Gali is a giant goanna from Yuwaalaraay folklore with a venomous bite.
claims.statement_id: Mungoon-Gali adalah biawak goanna raksasa dari cerita rakyat Yuwaalaraay yang meneror penduduk dengan gigitan berbisa.
claims.quote: Mungoon-Gali, also transcribed as Mungoongarlee, is a giant goanna from Yuwaalaraay Folklore who terrorised the local people with his venomous bite and voracious appetite.

claims.statement: In those days lizards were venomous instead of snakes, and Ouyouboolooey offered to steal the poison bag.
claims.statement_id: Pada zaman dahulu, biawaklah yang berbisa dan bukannya ular, lalu Ouyouboolooey menawarkan diri mencuri kantung bisa itu.
claims.quote: Afraid the tribes would soon be wiped out by the constant attacks, Ouyouboolooey the black snake offered to steal the hidden poison bag from Mungoon-Gali for in those days, it was lizards instead of snakes that were venomous.

claims.statement: Mungoon-Gali handed the poison bag to Ouyouboolooey who fled with it.
claims.statement_id: Mungoon-Gali menyerahkan kantung bisa dari mulutnya kepada Ouyouboolooey yang kemudian membawanya kabur.
claims.quote: Mungoon-Gali, reluctant but determined to learn of the plot against him, took the poison bag from his mouth and handed it Ouyouboolooey who placed it in his own and fled, easily outpacing the still sluggish reptile.

claims.statement: This explains how snakes became venomous and lizards lost their toxic bite.
claims.statement_id: Ouyouboolooey membawa kantung bisa ke semak belukar yang menjelaskan bagaimana ular menjadi berbisa dan biawak kehilangan bisanya.
claims.quote: On returning to the tribes, Ouyouboolooey refused to destroy the bag and instead retreated into the bush which explains how snakes become venomous and lizards, like the ferocious Mungoon-Gali, lost their bite.

claims.statement: Mungoongarlee, the largest kind of iguana, which even now in its dwarfed condition measures about five feet from tongue to tail, was quite a terror in the land because of his poisonous bite.
claims.statement_id: Mungoongarlee, iguana terbesar yang bahkan kini dalam wujudnya yang lebih kecil panjangnya sekitar lima kaki dari lidah hingga ekor, menjadi teror di negeri itu karena gigitannya yang beracun.
claims.quote: Mungoongarlee, the largest kind of iguana, which even now in its comparatively dwarfed condition measures five feet or so from tongue to tail, was, by reason of his poisonous bite, quite a terror in the land.

claims.statement: In those days the bite of a snake was not poisonous, but that of an iguana was.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa itu gigitan ular tidak beracun, tetapi gigitan iguana beracun.
claims.quote: In those days the bite of a snake was not poisonous, but that of an iguana was.

claims.statement: Such havoc had he wrought that at last all the other tribes held a meeting to discuss how best to check the wholesale slaughter.
claims.statement_id: Kerusakan yang ia timbulkan begitu besar sehingga akhirnya semua suku lain mengadakan pertemuan untuk membahas cara terbaik menghentikan pembantaian massal itu.
claims.quote: Such havoc had he wrought amongst them that at last all the other tribes held a meeting to discuss how best to check this wholesale slaughter.

claims.statement: Ever since then the snakes have been poisonous and not the iguanas, and there has been a feud between snakes and iguanas, who never meet without fighting.
claims.statement_id: Sejak saat itu ularlah yang beracun, bukan iguana, dan terjadi permusuhan antara ular dan iguana, yang tak pernah bertemu tanpa berkelahi.
claims.quote: Ever since then the snakes have been poisonous, and not the iguanas, and there has been a feud between the snakes and the iguanas, who never meet without fighting.

claims.statement: Mungoongarlee was a great wirreenun and knew of a plant which, if eaten after snakebite, made the poison powerless to kill or injure.
claims.statement_id: Mungoongarlee adalah wirreenun yang hebat dan mengetahui tanaman yang jika dimakan setelah gigitan ular membuat racunnya tak mampu membunuh atau melukai.
claims.quote: For Mungoongarlee was a great wirreenun, and he knew of a plant which if eaten after snakebite made the poison powerless to kill or injure.

claims.statement: Negunung is a bat in Australian myths who created the first woman to bring balance.
claims.statement_id: Negunung adalah kelelawar dalam mitologi yang menciptakan wanita pertama untuk mewujudkan keseimbangan alam.
claims.quote: نجوننج (الإنجليزية: Negunung) الخفاش في أساطير استراليا الذي خلق المرأة الأولى ليحقق التوازن في الطبيعة حيث لم يكن يوجد سوى الرجال.

claims.statement: According to the Wotjobaluk account of the creation of man, long ago Ngunung-ngunnut, the bat, who was a man, lived on the earth with others like him, and there was no difference between the sexes.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah Wotjobaluk tentang penciptaan manusia, dahulu Ngunung-ngunnut, si kelelawar yang adalah seorang laki-laki, hidup di bumi bersama yang lain seperti dia, dan belum ada perbedaan jenis kelamin.
claims.quote: The Wotjobaluk account of the creation of man says that long ago Ngunung-ngunnut, the bat, who was a man, lived on the earth, and there were others like him, but there was no difference between the sexes.

claims.statement: Feeling lonely, he wished for a wife and altered himself and one other so that he became the man and the other the woman.
claims.statement_id: Karena merasa kesepian, ia menginginkan seorang istri, lalu mengubah dirinya dan satu orang lain sehingga ia menjadi laki-laki dan yang lain menjadi perempuan.
claims.quote: Feeling lonely, he wished for a wife, and he altered himself and one other, so that he was the man and the other was the woman.

claims.statement: Then he made fire by rubbing a stick on a log of wood.
claims.statement_id: Setelah itu ia membuat api dengan menggosokkan sebatang kayu pada kayu gelondongan.
claims.quote: Then he made fire by rubbing a stick on a log of wood.

claims.statement: According to the Wurunjerri, Bunjil made men of clay and gave them life, while his brother Pallina, the bat, brought women up out of the water to be their wives.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah Wurunjerri, Bunjil membuat manusia dari tanah liat dan memberinya kehidupan, sedangkan saudaranya, Pallina si kelelawar, membawa perempuan naik dari air untuk menjadi istri mereka.
claims.quote: According to the Wurunjerri, it was Bunjil who made men of clay and imparted life to them, while his brother, Pallina, the bat, brought women up out of the water to be their wives.

claims.statement: A list of Australian Aboriginal mythological figures names Balayang, a bat deity and brother of Bunjil.
claims.statement_id: Daftar tokoh mitologi Aborigin menyebut Balayang, dewa kelelawar dan saudara Bunjil.
claims.quote: Balayang, bat deity and brother of Bunjil

claims.statement: Ngiṉṯaka is a mythological giant perentie lizard from Aṉangu and Pitjantjatjara Aboriginal religion.
claims.statement_id: Ngiṉṯaka atau Ngintaku adalah kadal perentie raksasa mitologis dari agama Aṉangu dan Pitjantjatjara.
claims.quote: Ngiṉṯaka (Aboriginal pronunciation: [ŋiɳʈaka]), also spelled Ngintaku, is a mythological giant perentie lizard from Aṉangu and Pitjantjatjara Aboriginal religion. It is associated with Angatja, an area along an important songline.

claims.statement: Ngiṉṯaka travels searching for a better grindstone in the myth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos, Ngiṉṯaka berkelana dari dekat perbatasan Western Australia menuju Oodnadatta mencari batu gerinda.
claims.quote: In the myth, Ngiṉṯaka travels from his home near the Western Australia border to the camp of another lizard tribe, near Oodnadatta, in search of a better grindstone.

claims.statement: As he travels, he creates many landforms in the Musgrave and Mann Ranges.
claims.statement_id: Saat berkelana, ia menciptakan banyak bentang alam di Musgrave and Mann Ranges dan memuntahkan benih tanaman pangan.
claims.quote: As he travels, he creates many landforms in the Musgrave and Mann Ranges and vomits up various grass seeds and vegetable foods.

claims.statement: The project has overcome controversy to preserve one of Central Australia's oldest intact songlines, the Ngintaka or Perentie Lizard dreaming.
claims.statement_id: Proyek ini mengatasi kontroversi untuk melestarikan salah satu songline tertua yang masih utuh di Australia Tengah, yaitu dreaming Ngintaka atau Perentie Lizard.
claims.quote: The endeavour has overcome controversy to preserve one of Central Australia's oldest intact songlines called the Ngintaka, or Perentie Lizard, dreaming.

claims.statement: The paintings showcase Ngintaka, the perenti lizard man, a mystical being at the heart of a creation story mapping outback lands.
claims.statement_id: Lukisan-lukisan itu menampilkan Ngintaka, manusia perenti (perenti lizard man), makhluk mistis di jantung kisah penciptaan yang memetakan wilayah pedalaman.
claims.quote: The paintings showcase Ngintaka - the perenti lizard man - a mystical being at the heart of a creation story mapping outback lands.

claims.statement: His is a tale of theft, deceit and vengeance: Ngintaka steals a grinding stone and flees, changing the landscape along the way and eventually being transformed into a mountain.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya adalah kisah pencurian, tipu daya, dan balas dendam: Ngintaka mencuri batu gerinda lalu kabur, mengubah bentang alam di sepanjang jalan, dan akhirnya berubah menjadi gunung.
claims.quote: His is a tale of theft, deceit, and vengeance, involving Ngintaka stealing a grinding stone and fleeing, changing the landscape along the way and eventually being transformed himself into a mountain.

claims.statement: Generations of Aboriginal people known as Anangu have learned the Ngintaka tale, and how he created food sources and waterholes still found today, through a musical story called a songline.
claims.statement_id: Generasi demi generasi orang Aborigin yang dikenal sebagai Anangu mempelajari kisah Ngintaka, dan bagaimana ia menciptakan sumber makanan serta lubang air yang masih ada kini, lewat kisah bermusik yang disebut songline.
claims.quote: Generations of Aboriginal people known as Anangu have learned the Ngintaka tale - and how he created food sources and waterholes still found today - through a musical story called a songline.

claims.statement: Elder Inawinytji Williamson says the Ngintaka story is one of the most important to Anangu.
